attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Litigation - Plaintiff - All Types of Personal Injury Cases Lawyers in East Syracuse, NY
attorneys.bio:
Described by his clients as an attorney of the “highest quality” who goes “above and beyond”, Jeff DeFrancisco, Esq. has made a career achieving top results for his clients. As a lifelong resident of Upstate, New York, Jeff DeFrancisco has earned a reputation of being a top attorney in his field of medical malpractice and personal injury. Jeff DeFrancisco handles cases all throughout New York State with the exception of down state.

Attorney DeFrancisco has achieved some of the top results known in Upstate, New York. A few examples of his many achievements include:

PARALYSIS: $10,000,000 jury verdict following a 3-week trial against 3 defense lawyers for a case where an individual became paralyzed due to medical malpractice.

BRAIN INJURY: $17,500,000 in payments: $3,000,000 cash; $12,000,000 expected payout between a lump sum payment and lifetime monthly payments to an individual who sustained a brain injury; and $2,500,000 in guaranteed lifetime payments to the child of the injured.

PARALYSIS: $11,200,000 unanimous arbitration award involving a patient that is paralyzed.

BIRTH INJURY: $5,600,000 which includes 2 lump sum cash payouts; $3,600,000 in tax free cash payments to the injured child for life; and the injured child was received into the Medical Indemnity Fund (MIF) which will cover all of the medical needs of the child for life.

FAILURE TO DIAGNOSE / INJECTION INJURY: $2,250,000 for a case that was turned down by another law firm. Jeff actually found 2 viable medical malpractice cases. One case settled for $250,000 and the other case settled for $2,000,000.

MEDICAL MALPRACTICE: $1,690,000 jury verdict for a medical malpractice case. The insurance company refused to offer any compensation. This matter was appealed to the highest appeal court in New York and the verdict was upheld.

WRONGFUL DEATH: $1,600,000 jury verdict on a wrongful death case that was turned down by two medical malpractice law firms. Jeff took the case to trial and got a fair result for the family.

CANCER MALPRACTICE: $1,400,000 settlement for failing to timely diagnose and appropriately treat cancer.

CANCER MALPRACTICE: $1,300,000 for failing to timely diagnose prostate cancer.

AUTO / TRUCKING ACCIDENT: $1,000,000 settlement.

In addition to the above, Attorney DeFrancisco has successfully resolved many other million and multi-million dollar cases. More results can be seen on his website: www.defranciscolaw.com

Jeff DeFrancisco, Esq. is also a member a member of SuperLawyers, the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum, Best Lawyers/Best Law Firms, and Best Attorneys of America, among other memberships.

Attorney DeFrancisco has extensive experience handling all different types of personal injury matters including medical malpractice, birth injuries, brain injuries, spinal cord injuries, cancer cases, wrongful death, and general personal injury cases such as automobile and truck accidents. Because his practice is devoted to representing the injured and their families, he is extremely knowledgeable of the medicine and human anatomy.

If you are seriously injured, call the lawyer who has a proven track record of obtaining top results in personal injury and medical malpractice cases. Call today for a free consultation.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Kew Gardens, NY
attorneys.bio:
Prior to opening his own practice, Mr. DeFelice worked as a Law Secretary to Supreme Court Justices, an Assistant District Attorney in Queens County and an Attorney with the Immigration and Naturalization Service. He is admitted to the New York and Florida Bar, United States District Courts for the Southern and Eastern Districts of New York, the U.S. Circuit Courts of Appeal for the 2nd, 3rd, and 11th Districts and the U.S. Supreme Court.

Mr DeFelice is a graduate of St John’s University – B.A. in Political Science 1970 and St. John’s Law School – J.D. 1973. He has handled an extensive amount of appeals and trials including numerous murder cases and was qualified as an Associate Counsel to handle Capital trials. Mr. DeFelice is active with the local bar association in Queens County where he is co-chairman of the Appellate Practice Committee and the Immigration and Naturalization Committee. He has served as President of the Confederation of Columbian Lawyers and President of the Columbian Lawyers, Queens County, has lectured at various CLE programs in Criminal and Immigration Law and Appeals for St John’s Law School and the Queens County Bar Assn. and participated in Mock Trial tournaments as a Judge in nationwide competition of college students. He also assisted in the formation of the Bridge the Gap program offered by the Educational Programs Committee of the Alumni Assn at St. John’s School of Law. Mr. DeFelice currently serves as a member of the Grievance Committee for the 2nd, 11th and 13th Judicial Districts in Brooklyn, New York and on the Members Benefit Committee for the Florida Bar.

Mr. DeFelice co-authored a discussion which appeared in the Journal of Forensic Science that relates to issues concerning the shaking baby syndrome. He has written a chapter entitled Immigration Remedies for the Battered Spouse which appears in a Domestic Violence book recently published by the New York State Bar Assn. He also wrote an article on the Freedom of Information Law relating to one of his appeals which appeared in the Criminal Law News and wrote an article concerning the jury system which appeared in the New York Law Journal in May, 2005.

Some of his appeals include- People v Parks, 95 NY2d 811; People v Alfonso, 63 NY2d 419; DeFelice ex rel. Barbera v NY City Police Dept., 89 NY2d 267; People v LaPene, 40 NY2d 210; People v Haupt, 71 NY2d 929; People v Brown, 30 AD3d 561; Francis v INS - 2nd Circuit Court of Appeals; Perez v INS, - 2nd Circuit Court of Appeals; Aziz v Dept. of Homeland Security, USDC, EDNY; Josan v Josan, 134 AD2d 486 and Kromer v Kromer, 177 AD2d 472.

attorneys.name: Michael P. DeGroat
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Walton, NY
attorneys.bio:
Michael P. DeGroat became of counsel to Coughlin & Gerhart, LLP on January 1, 2014, after having spent 35 years practicing law in Delaware County, New York. From 1978 to 1980 Mike served as law assistant to Delaware County Judge Richard H. Farley. In 1980, he joined the firm of Eaton, Griffith and Mugglin. Mike has maintained a general practice of law in Walton since that time, concentrating in the areas of real estate, estate planning, estate administration, and banking law. He has also been the town attorney for the Town of Colchester in Delaware County since 1988. Mike has been affiliated with many Delaware County entities. He was a director of Delaware Valley Hospital, Inc. and has been director of The National Bank of Delaware County. He also served as a member of the Independent Judicial Election Qualification Commission. He is a member of the New York State Bar Association and the Delaware County and Broome County Bar Associations.

Mike and his wife Jean reside in Walton, New York. Mike is a parishioner and a lector at St. John the Baptist Roman Catholic Church. He is a veteran of the United States Army.

attorneys.name: Gamaliel Delgado
attorneys.practice_type: Brain Injuries Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Gamaliel B. Delgado is a trial attorney focusing on premises liability cases in the Manhattan office. A native New Yorker from the Bronx, of Puerto Rican heritage, he obtained a Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science from the University of Massachusetts at Amherst and his Juris Doctor degree from Rutgers University School of Law, Newark. While in law school, he was a finalist in the Nathan Baker Moot Court Competition, and went on to be a Semi-Finalist in the National Mock Trial Competition. Following his graduation from law school, he has been a partner at a prominent law firm in New York City and New Jersey.

Gamaliel is an accomplished trial attorney with significant litigation experience over the course of the last 15 years. He focuses his personal injury practice in the areas of premises liability, construction accidents, wrongful death, motor vehicle collisions, assaults, negligent security, burn injuries, dog bites, and general liability matters in New York State and Federal Courts. Gamaliel is admitted to practice before the courts of the states of New York and New Jersey, the United States District Courts for the Southern and Eastern Districts of New York and the District of New Jersey. He is also admitted to the bar of the United States Supreme Court.

When not working, Gamaliel values giving back to the community, focusing on increasing the diversity pipeline for future generations. He is a Regional Deputy President of the Hispanic National Bar Association, where he has been involved for a number of years in developing programing, including mentorship events for law students and public speaking competitions for elementary school students.

Gamaliel Delgado became an attorney because he believes in justice for those who are often looked over by the legal system. He considers it a privilege to represent the people, not the powerful.

attorneys.name: Anthony M. Deliso
attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle Accidents Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Anthony Deliso is a senior labor law attorney in the Manhattan office of The Barnes Firm. Anthony is an accomplished personal injury attorney, serving as an associate for 7 years at a personal injury firm in Brooklyn, followed by 6 years as a senior partner at a firm in Manhattan, where he was the Chair of The Labor Law Department and oversaw a team of 6 attorneys. During this time, he obtained numerous partial summary judgement awards and successfully argued before the Appellate Division.

Anthony’s passion for representing and protecting union members, from all trades, comes from his grandfather. As the grandson of a union ornamental iron worker who worked on some of the City’s most iconic structures, buildings, and monuments, including, the Statute of Liberty, Anthony has dedicated his career to using his voice to advocate for those individuals who have been injured due to someone else’s negligence on a jobsite.

With over 20 years of legal experience, his understanding of construction and personal injury law has helped him resolve over $50M in cases.

Anthony’s commitment to understanding the unique challenges faced by victims of construction accidents, highlight his dedication to securing compensation and holding responsible parties accountable. His history of achieving successful outcomes in a variety of construction accident cases reflects his commitment to achieving justice for his clients.

attorneys.name: Carol G. Dell
attorneys.practice_type: Labor & Employee Benefits Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Determined and persistent advocate for clients’ interests.

Carol G. Dell is as steadfast in promoting her clients’ positions in negotiations, court proceedings, and formal hearings as she is meticulous in preparing the legal documents, plan documents, and motions to support them. She is committed to advising clients of the constantly changing and evolving laws and regulations that affect clients.

Ms. Dell works with union, governmental, and multi-employer pension and benefit plans. She also serves as counsel to a number of unions and related Taft-Hartley and governmental funds. Ms. Dell represents collective bargaining units and their associated benefit funds in various labor law matters, as well as employment law matters.

Ms. Dell’s clients retain and rely on her to:

Monitor and enforce ERISA requirements.

Advise on compliance matters involving multi-employer benefit plans, public sector benefit plans, retirement plans [(Defined Contribution (DC) and Defined Benefit (DB)], and Welfare Plans.

Form and structure benefit plans.

Provide representation in arbitrations, grievance mediations and hearings, administrative proceedings and litigation involving unions and benefit funds.

Provide representation in ERISA litigation and collection actions.

Represent fund trustees in ERISA and other fiduciary matters.

Advise on Withdrawal Liability matters.

Negotiate collective bargaining agreements on behalf of unions (private sector and public sector).

Provide representation in NLRB, EEOC and NY Human Rights Division proceedings concerning duty of fair representation issues, elections, employment discrimination claims and unfair labor practices claims.

Advocate in Bankruptcy actions in which her clients are creditors.

attorneys.name: Joseph G. Dell
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Accidents & Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Garden City, NY
attorneys.bio:
Joseph Dell, the firm's Managing Member and President, is regarded as one of New York's top trial lawyers and a zealous advocate of those injured through the negligence of others.

Having started the firm with the singular goal of leveling the playing field for those injured, Mr. Dell has worked tirelessly for his clients since its inception over two (2) decades ago.

In addition to managing the firm and trying cases, he is a frequent lecturer at law school and Bar Associations on cases of significant importance in the negligence field. In particular, the law-changing win in Davis v. South Nassau Communities Hospital is just one of the many cases and topics he speaks about.

He has been recognized for his career of accomplishment with his induction into the New York Metro Area Super Lawyers; Top 10 Personal Injury Lawyers in New York; Best of Long Island; Top Verdict and Settlement List for New York; The Nation's Top One Percent as well as the Top 100 Litigation Lawyers in the State of New York.

Currently, Mr. Dell serves on the Board of Governors of Touro College - Jacob D. Fuchsberg Law Center. He is a prior member of the Board of Directors of the New York State Trial Lawyers Association and remains as an active committee member. He is a member of the New York State Academy of Trial Lawyers. He is a Member of the American Association for Justice, and the Southern Poverty Law Center. He is also a sustaining member of the Nassau County Bar Association.

Mr. Dell graduated from St. John's University's College of Business Administration Cum Laude in 1988. He then attended and graduated from St. John's University School of Law in 1991.

Admitted to the New York State Bar in 1992 as well as the Federal District Courts for both the Eastern and Southern Districts of New York.

He has successfully argued Davis v. South Nassau Communities Hospital in 2015 before the New York Court of Appeals, forever changing the medical malpractice landscape in New York.

Over the past twenty-five (25) years, he has recovered by both verdicts and settlements totaling hundreds of millions of dollars for injured plaintiffs and their families.

His proudest recognition is the loyalty and love he receives from his clients and their families. These relationships have grown out of his dedication, respect and concern for each client of his firm.

The firm's mantra that when you hire Dell & Dean you become part of the D2 family is not just an expression, it is the philosophy that permeates the entire firm culture. He meets each client of the firm and gets to know them, their families and understands what each client needs from their case. This type of personalized attention and bond gives him the ability to go above and beyond for each client of the firm.

As most colleagues and clients already know, Mr. Dell is often still in the office every night until 10:00p.m., returning every call he has received that day. He believes strongly that every call and email deserves a response.

Joseph Dell resides on Long Island with his wife and children.

attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law and Estate Planning Lawyers in Staten Island, NY
attorneys.bio:
Stefanie Lynn DeMario-Germershausen, partner at Angiuli & Gentile, LLP, has over 13 years of experience and leads the firm’s Estates, Trusts, Real Estate and Medicaid Departments. Her areas of concentration include probate and administration of estates, estate litigation and both 17A and Article 81 guardianship proceedings.

Additional areas of concentration for Ms. DeMario-Germershausen include estate planning and special needs planning along with assisting clients in obtaining Veteran’s benefits.

Ms. DeMario-Germershausen prides herself on helping clients achieve Medicaid eligibility, having handled complex community and institutional Medicaid cases and Fair Hearings. Her expertise with both the Medicaid rules and regulations makes her a go to attorney for both emergency and structured Medicaid planning.

Within the Real Estate Department Ms. DeMario-Germershausen guides clients as she helps them navigate sale and purchase transactions. She and her team understand that for many clients the sale of their family home or the purchase of their forever home are some of the most pivotal moments in their lives. Understanding that no two transactions are the same, Ms. DeMario-Germershausen and the entire Real Estate Department make sure to handle each transaction with a personal touch and strategic coordination.

Ms. DeMario-Germershausen is a highly accomplished attorney and was awarded the prestigious designation of “Rising Star” attorney by Super Lawyers.

Ms. DeMario-Germershausen received her Juris Doctor (J.D.) in 2011 from New York Law School and is admitted to the New York State Bar, the New Jersey Bar and the United States District Court of New Jersey. As a St. John’s University alumna, she earned her Bachelor of Science degree while serving as the President of the University’s Moot Court Association and maintaining Dean’s List status.

Ms. DeMario-Germershausen is a current board member of the Staten Island Chamber of Commerce. She has served as the co-chair of the Staten Island Chamber of Commerce’s Young Professionals Group as well as the Secretary of the Chamber’s Business Guild III.

attorneys.name: James R. Denlea
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in White Plains, NY
attorneys.bio:
Upon graduation from law school, Jim became a Westchester County Assistant District Attorney. Due to a prosecutor's exemption, he won his first jury trial before he was informed that he passed the Bar exam. That victory began a distinguished thirty year career as a trial attorney, as notable for the diversity of cases tried, as it has been for Jim's success before a jury.

Among Jim's many professional accomplishments, are a $5.6 million verdict in a propane explosion case; representing the trustees of the estate of renowned diet doctor Dr. Robert Atkins; prosecuting the wrongful death action of Baltimore Orioles pitcher Steve Bechler, and serving as lead defense counsel in the consolidated tort actions concerning the capsizing of the Ethan Allen tour boat on Lake George, an action involving twenty fatalities.

Jim's abilities as a trial lawyer have enabled him to litigate both plaintiffs' and defense actions with equal dexterity. As a plaintiff's attorney (involving non-medical malpractice cases), Jim has secured awards of $3.5 million for a roofer who fell from a slate roof; a $7 million recovery for a corporation after a fire loss; and multiple recoveries in excess of one million dollars for victims of sexual abuse, burn cases, and motor vehicle accidents.

As a defense lawyer, Jim is regularly requested to personally represent physicians throughout the state. The scope of this representation includes defending physicians in malpractice actions, as well as representing their interests before the Office of Professional Medical Conduct (OPMC) and in investigations conducted by the Department of Health and the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

In the field of intellectual property, Jim has obtained a million dollar settlement in a patent action. He represented the interests of an international manufacturer of engineering components in Lanham Act claims involving numerous infringements upon the company's trademarks. He also assists physicians in protecting their intellectual property involving new medical devices and the expanded utilization of existing technology. Jim was also responsible for the development of proprietary software that enabled a national insurance company to dramatically reduce losses due to fraudulent claims.

Most recently, Jim successfully argued an appeal before the Second Circuit Court of Appeals, which overturned a District Court ruling involving issues of standing and interstate commerce.

Jim is a Fellow of the American Bar Foundation, a perennial Super Lawyer, as well as a lifetime member of the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates and Elite Lawyers. While such recognition from his peers is appreciated, Jim has always found the connection with a client, for whom he has obtained a life-altering result, to be far more rewarding.

He has assisted a number of Fortune 500 companies to implement patent programs, including mining the company’s technology to prime and sustain the program, as well as setting up infrastructure necessary to support the program. He routinely performs IP due diligence for clients making acquisitions or investments in technology companies, and advises clients on how to deal with patent portfolios of competitors and patent holding companies. Mr. DeRosa also prepares and prosecutes patent applications, and his practice also includes licensing, litigation, and trademark law.

Mr. DeRosa has expertise in the technical areas of computers, software, Internet, electronics, and electro-mechanical devices. Before attending law school, he practiced as an electrical engineer for six years, and has first-hand experience working with scientists and engineers.

Mr. DeRosa has extensive experience in patenting and counseling on business methods and software for financial services, insurance products, advertising, and the Internet.

Frank DeRosa has been listed in the New York Super Lawyers 2007-2009, and in Chambers USA 2007 (as one of the leading intellectual property lawyers in New York).

attorneys.name: Jeffrey DeRoberts
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Syracuse, NY
attorneys.bio:
Jeffrey DeRoberts has been dealing with the family and matrimonial laws of New York since becoming an attorney back in 1993. As a solo attorney, he can provide the personalized attention you may not get at a larger firm. There is no substitute for one-on-one contact and accessibility from your attorney, particularly in difficult situations involving your family.

Because of Mr. DeRoberts' focused knowledge with child custody, child support and divorce, he can often resolve your dispute quicker and more cost-effectively than a larger law firm. He is supported by two dedicated paralegals, but he personally attends to the details of your case, including being at your side for all hearings or negotiation sessions. He offers you his experience, dedication and personal attention throughout the duration of your case.

We handle all family court matters in Onondaga County and surrounding areas of Central New York, from Syracuse, Auburn and Ithaca to Binghamton, Utica and Watertown.

Special Experience in Post-Divorce Disputes

Long after your divorce is finalized and you have settled into your new life, circumstances may change. The other parent may not be allowing you the scheduled amount of visitation. You may wish to go back to school, take a new job or relocate. You may need additional financial support to provide for the needs of your growing and active child.

Jeffrey DeRoberts devotes a large portion of his practice to modification hearings to alter custody, child support or spousal support and helping clients enforce visitation or child support orders.

We can, of course, also represent your interests in your New York divorce, assuring fair treatment in property division or a marital separation agreement.

Out-of-State Clients

Many of our clients are non-custodial parents whose visitation rights are gradually degraded by the parent who has primary custody. We can represent parents who have relocated beyond Central New York or even out of state, reasserting your rights in contempt proceedings so that your relationship with your children remains strong despite the distance between you.

attorneys.name: John M Desiderio
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Litigation Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
John M. Desiderio has been a practicing attorney in New York City for over forty years. His practice is concentrated in real estate litigation, antitrust and trade regulation, intellectual property, and food and drug law.

Mr. Desiderio received his A.B. degree from Fordham College in 1963, an LL.B. degree from the University of Pennsylvania Law School in 1966, and an LL.M. degree from New York University School of Law in 1969. He served as a Captain in U.S. Army Intelligence from 1966 to 1968.

From 1969 to 1980, Mr. Desiderio was an Assistant New York State Attorney General under Attorneys General Louis Lefkowitz and Robert Abrams, and from 1972 to 1980 he served as Chief of the Attorney General's Anti-Monopolies (now Antitrust) Bureau.

Mr. Desiderio entered private practice in 1981 and represented clients in antitrust, RICO, real estate, and general civil litigation. From 1989 to February 1999, he was a member of the firm of Bass & Ullman, P.C.

He has extensive experience in conducting and defending depositions and in conducting trials and arguing appeals in both New York State and federal courts. In addition to his many court appearances within New York State, Mr. Desiderio has appeared in and argued matters in the federal courts in Atlanta, Birmingham, Chicago, Hartford, Knoxville, Los Angeles, Newark, Philadelphia, San Francisco, and Washington, D.C., and he has appeared in and argued, pro hac vice, at both the trial court and appellate levels in the courts of the State of Illinois.

Mr. Desiderio's reported cases include: Nutritional Health Alliance v. Food and Drug Administration, 318 F3d 92 (2d Cir.2003); Million Gold Realty Co. v. SE&K Corp., 4 AD3d 196, 772 NYS2d 271 (1st Dept. 2004); Anthony Gangi v. Solgar Co., Inc., 267 AD2d 350, 699 NYS2d 922 (2d Dept. 1999); Alleghany Pharmacal Corporation, et al v. Parbel of Florida, Inc., 226 AD2d 104, 640 NYS2d 507 (1st Dept. 1996); Shulton, Inc. v. Optel Corporation, et al, 698 F. Supp. 61 (D.N.J. 1988); Frank Saltz & Sons, Inc. v. Hart Schaffner & Marx, 1985-2 Trade Cas. (CCH) 66,768 (S.D.N.Y. 1985).

Mr. Desiderio's has published articles on issues involving real estate law, antitrust law, and food and drug law.

Mr. Desiderio is rated "AV" by Martindale-Hubbell and is listed in the Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers.

Mr. Desiderio was elected to the Board of Governors of the Columbus Citizens Foundation in 2008.

Rory Deutsch is head of the firm’s tax practice and counsel to the firm’s corporate and securities practice. Mr. Deutsch founded the firm, together with Messrs. Wollmuth and Maher in April 1998. Rory’s practice focuses on providing corporate and tax guidance to clients on domestic and international corporate transactional matters including mergers and acquisitions, securities offerings, private equity and venture capital formation, acquisition and financing transactions, debt and equity financings, hedge fund representation, counseling of early-stage and middle-market companies, derivative transactions, structuring of executive employment and incentive compensation agreements, procurement of Internal Revenue Service private letter rulings and technical advice memoranda, and resolution of federal and state tax disputes.

attorneys.name: Michael C. Deutsch
attorneys.practice_type: Securities and Commodities Arbitration Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Michael C. Deutsch - a Georgetown University Law Center graduate - is a Partner with, and Co Founder of, Singer Deutsch LLP. A Member of both the New York and New Jersey Bars, he co founded Singer Deutsch LLP after working for over 8 years at Eclipse Sports Management (previously Impact Sports Management), a sports agency he founded with Scott Greenspun, Esq. Mr. Deutsch has negotiated numerous multi million dollar contracts for professional ice hockey players from around the world, and has represented players in salary arbitrations conducted under the auspices of the NHL Collective Bargaining Agreement. He continues to represent athletes in conjunction with his securities and employment law practice at Singer Deutsch LLP.

In connection with his nationwide employment law practice, Mr. Deutsch represents high-level individuals affiliated primarily with the Securities and Commodities industries, such as Wall Street traders, brokers, investment bankers, financial planners, wholesalers, compliance personnel, operations personnel, hedge fund executives, private equity fund executives, hedge fund marketers, and research analysts. Mr. Deutsch represents these individuals in both arbitrations and litigations against their former employers and in investigations or enforcement proceedings conducted by the Securities and Commodities regulators. With respect to Mr. Deutsch's nationwide representation of Securities and Commodities professionals against their former employers, the claims typically involve bonus disputes, wrongful terminations, U-5 defamation, failures to pay compensation (oftentimes involving stock options), whistle-blowing, discrimination, harassment, and slander. These actions are typically arbitrated at the NYSE or NASD; they are sometimes arbitrated and/or mediated at the AAA and JAMS as well. Mr. Deutsch's clients range in title from Associate to Senior Managing Director. Mr. Deutsch also represents NASD and NYSE member firms against other member firms in disputes emanating from unlawful solicitations, tortious interferences with business relations, and trading errors.

With respect to Mr. Deutsch's nationwide representation of Securities and Commodities professionals who are under investigation by the Securities and Commodities regulators, the issues range from market-timing, late-day trading, front-running and unauthorized, outside business activities to sales-practices issues (unsuitability and churning), forgery, and insider trading. Mr. Deutsch also negotiates multi-million dollar (and other) employment agreements and separation/severance agreements for his clients. Mr. Deutsch also represents high-profile individuals in the entertainment industry including, but not limited to, senior record label executives, models, actresses, and world renowned authors, as well as high-profile individuals in other industries, in connection with employment disputes with their former employers, contract negotiations, and commercial litigation disputes.

In connection with his nationwide representation of individual investors, Mr. Deutsch handles diverse, complex matters against investment banks, brokerage firms, hedge funds, financial planners, and investment advisors emanating from investment-related losses. These matters typically involve unsuitable investing, breaches of fiduciary duties, negligence, churning, material misrepresentations, unauthorized trading, material omissions, failures to supervise, blue-sky violations, and fraud. Mr. Deutsch represents these individual investors nationwide in NYSE, NASD, NFA, AAA, and JAMS Arbitrations.

Prior to his formation of Singer Deutsch LLP, and on a continuing basis, Mr. Deutsch - in connection with his work at Eclipse Sports Management - has negotiated multi-million dollar contracts for professional ice hockey players throughout the world, including those in the NHL, Russian Elite League, Czech Extraliga, Finnish SM-Liiga, Swedish Elitserien and the German Elite League. His clients in North America have played for the New York Rangers, New York Islanders, New Jersey Devils, Boston Bruins, Chicago Blackhawks, Nashville Predators, Anaheim Ducks, Dallas Stars, Colorado Avalanche, Florida Panthers, Toronto Maple Leafs, Vancouver Canucks and Ottawa Senators, among others.

Mr. Deutsch also practiced law from 1996 through 2002 at the New York City firm Braverman & Associates, where he was a commercial litigator.

Mr. Deutsch previously served on the Board of Directors of Red Star Asset Management, a New York/Moscow based hedge fund.

On March 29, 2005, Mr. Deutsch served as a Panel Member on the National Association of Independent Broker Dealers Forum for "Arbitration & Mediation." www.naibd.com/events.htm.

Mr. Deutsch has been a guest lecturer regarding the NHL Collective Bargaining Agreement at both New York University and Adelphi University.

Mr. Deutsch is a member of Team Continuum, Inc., an organization comprised of individuals who run marathons to raise money for cancer patients.

Mr. Deutsch, an active NASD arbitrator, is a Member of the New York and New Jersey Bars, along with various federal courts, and is a member of the Public Investors Arbitration Association (PIABA) and the Bar Association of the City of New York. He received his undergraduate degree from Georgetown University in 1988, and his law degree from the Georgetown University Law Center in 1992.

For more than 20 years, Jed Dietrich, the President of Dietrich Law Firm P.C., has consistently exemplified an aggressive, straightforward and eminently prepared approach to the practice of law. This has led to Mr. Dietrich's clients obtaining exceptional results.

These successes have led to Mr. Dietrich's invitation, and admission, into the Million Dollar Advocates Forum, a specialized group of attorneys who have distinguished themselves by achieving substantial results on behalf of their clients.

Mr. Dietrich's background initially started in the athletic world. He was an International Champion in the sport of rowing. Throughout Mr. Dietrich's rowing career, which spanned a decade, he represented the United States in Czechoslovakia, England and Canada. Mr. Dietrich was recognized (while a U.S citizen) as the Canadian Sculler of the Year in 1992 for his outstanding accomplishments at the Canadian Henley Rowing Regatta where he won the top 3 races in the Heavyweight Single Division, setting course records in every event. He was also a National Collegiate Champion, 3 years in a row, in the Varsity Heavyweight 8 while studying for his undergraduate degree at Temple University in Philadelphia.

The main precept that Mr. Dietrich learned throughout his days as a competitive oarsman, is the fact that nothing can replace hard work and dedication when it comes to obtaining the best possible results. As the driving force behind The Dietrich Law Firm, Mr. Dietrich mandates that every claim be handled with the same level of enthusiasm.

The Dietrich Law Firm P.C. pledges and commits that every effort will be made to prosecute your claim aggressively and vigorously to obtain the compensation that you deserve.

attorneys.name: Gary M Dimuzio
attorneys.practice_type: Mesothelioma & Asbestos Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Gary DiMuzio is a partner in the Asbestos Department at Simmons Hanly Conroy. He joined the firm in 2019, bringing 25 years of experience helping victims of mesothelioma and other environmental and workplace hazards. During his career, Gary has represented plaintiffs in cases involving mesothelioma, lung cancer, leukemia, liver cancer, silicosis, plant explosions and environmental contamination.

Based in the firm's New York office, Gary has been litigating mesothelioma cases since 1998. As a trial attorney, he handles every aspect of the litigation process, from client intake to discovery, to motion practice through trial verdict, working to achieve justice for his clients, anywhere in the country.

"I will first work with the litigation team to learn a client's story, then contact them to get additional insight and prepare them for trial," Gary said. "All of us will work together to give the client their best possible day in court and the best result for them and their family."

Success at Trial

Gary is a skilled legal advocate for his clients and has secured impressive and continuing results. During his legal tenure, Gary has served as first and second chair during trials that resulted in multi-million-dollar results, representing individuals suffering from mesothelioma due to exposure from machinery, automobiles, insulators, sheetrock, refineries, industrial workplaces and respirators. He has also handled cases involving secondary/household exposure. Gary has fought for the spouses and children of workers who were exposed to the deadly dust brought home by workers and diagnosed decades later.

In November 2020, as lead attorney, Gary secured a $10.3 million verdict against two stevedoring companies and a shipping company on behalf of Henry Pete, who was diagnosed with mesothelioma in 2019. Henry was exposed to raw asbestos he unloaded from the Port of New Orleans while working as a longshoreman in the 1960s. Along with Gary, firm shareholders Michael K. Hibey, Melissa Crowe Schopfer and Jean-Michel LeCointre represented the family in the Civil District Court for the Parish of Orleans.

In 2016, Gary secured a nearly $5 million verdict for Vera Letha Adams, the widow of Perry Adams, against John Crane Inc. Perry passed away from mesothelioma in 2012 after previously testifying against John Crane Inc. and other defendants. The jury found John Crane liable for Perry's exposure to products containing asbestos during a nearly 20-year career, working at the Mahrt paper mill in Alabama.

"Many mesothelioma victims have never filed a lawsuit and thought they would never do so," Gary said. "In the process of dealing with a diagnosis of mesothelioma and its impact on every aspect of their lives, these men and women learn for the first time that not only could their past work have been the source of asbestos exposure, the dangers of such exposure were widely known among experts and the industry since at least 1930. But rather than risk profits, workers were put at risk."

In addition to handling asbestos cases, Gary has experience litigating cases involving hydrofluoric acid, PAHs, crude oil wastes, TCE, vinyl chloride, styrene tars, creosote and silica. His standout results include:

Prosecuting large environmental Superfund, chemical and explosion cases, as well as silicosis, benzene, hard metal disease and other toxic exposure injuries.

Drafting successful amicus briefs to various state supreme courts on causation methodology.

Designing and coordinating the execution of a large environmental epidemiology study.

Spearheading the statewide Utah MDL causation hearing, leading to a denial of the defendants' motion to adopt the Borg-Warner v. Flores Texas decision requiring quantification of exposure.

Successfully defending asbestos experts in the first State of Georgia Daubert challenge hearing.

In addition to these victories in courtrooms coast to coast, Gary has litigated hundreds of other cases against some of the nation's largest corporations and the scientists they hire to defend them. On a daily basis, he secures significant settlements for the firm's clients and their families in these additional cases before a trial or a verdict is warranted.Background and Experience

Gary entered law school with the goal of helping those poisoned by pollution, concentrating his studies on environmental and occupational contamination law. As a law student and legal intern for the Environmental Defense Fund, he drafted the fund's first successful lawsuit in Texas.

"My early experience seeing law, science and policy interface created the impetus to understand sciences such as toxicology, epidemiology, biostatics, environmental studies, risk assessment and exposure assessment in order to be the best advocate for my clients," he said.

With this underlying objective, Gary undertook environmental public health studies at the University of Texas School of Public Health concurrently with his law degree. He also worked on environmental issues with the Harris County Attorney's Office Environmental Division/Harris County Pollution Controls lawyers and experts, as well as researching how the courts judged causation science and toxic tort experts for the University of Houston Environmental Liability Law Program.

Before joining the firm, Gary served as of counsel at a Virginia firm while also managing his own Texas-based firm.

Gary received a B.M. in Classical Guitar Performance from Texas A&M University in 1986. He received his J.D. from University of Houston Law Center in 1992.

attorneys.name: Thomas J. DiNovo
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Latham, NY
attorneys.bio:
Tom is a partner in our Litigation department and practices almost exclusively in the area of Personal Injury Litigation. He represents clients who have sustained serious injuries as a result of accidents, product liability and professional malpractice in both State and Federal Courts. He has secured several multi-million dollar verdicts and settlements throughout New York and neighboring states. He is involved in the representation of clients at examinations before trial, various court proceedings and as trial counsel. He is known for his thoroughness and attention to detail, particularly in handling complex product liability and professional negligence matters.

Tom has lectured at seminars sponsored by the New York State Bar Association on various topics regarding personal injury litigation, and has also lectured to the National Academy of Forensic Engineers on topics including the use of forensic animation and expert witness testimony. He has co-authored articles on forensic animation for the Journal of the National Academy of Forensic Engineers.

Since 2017 Tom has consistently been named to the Upstate New York Super Lawyers list, a distinction earned by less that 5% of attorneys in the state. He has consecutively earned an "AV-Preeminent" rating by Martindale-Hubbell, the highest possible rating in both legal ability and ethical standards. He is a regular guest commentator on local radio shows, including TALK 1300 AM. As a Certified New York State Emergency Medical Technician, Tom is personally committed to supporting Emergency Service Providers in our local community. He acts as general counsel to several local emergency response organizations and has also provided continuing education programs to a number of EMS organizations and fire departments.

Very active in the community, Tom has served for many years on the Board and then Executive Board for local little league organizations. He serves as a member of the Board of Trustees at Christian Brothers Academy, and an all-boys LaSallian Jr/Sr high school. His community service activities also included volunteering to present safety programs to local high school students as part of a national End Districted Driving campaign.

attorneys.name: Kathleen ("Casey") Copps DiPaola
attorneys.practice_type: Adoption Lawyers in Albany, NY
attorneys.bio:
Casey focuses her practice in all areas of adoption law. She has experience representing birth and adoptive parents in private adoptions, voluntary agency adoptions, foster care adoptions and step/second parent adoptions. Casey also has experience representing adoption agencies and handling adoption subsidy fair hearings. Casey also practices in the related area of assisted reproductive technology law (egg/sperm/embryo donation and surrogacy/gestational carrier agreements) and kinship guardianship (KinGAP). Casey also practices in the areas of not-for-profit/for-profit/religious corporation formation and operations, estate planning and trusts, probate, real estate, landlord/tenant, employment law, education law and name changes.

Casey understands that many of her clients come to her during difficult and stressful times in their lives. She strives to educate her clients on the law and their options so they can make educated decisions about the trajectory of their cases. Casey understands that, while the matter that brings her clients to her are incredibly important to them, the vast majority of her clients have limited funds to spend on legal representation. With that in mind, Casey openly discusses with her clients the relative costs of various options and helps them to engage in a cost-benefit analysis.

Casey prides herself on being a creative problem solver and refuses to take a one size fits all approach to her cases. She spends time with her clients getting to know the facts of their cases intimately so she can help them brainstorm possible solutions to the problem that brought them to her. Particularly in matters involving families, Casey believes that working together to come up with a solution that addresses the needs and concerns of all involved to the best extent possible is almost always preferable to litigation, which can do irreparable damage to relationships. That being said, Casey has extensive litigation experience and, in the event that settlement is not an option, she is willing and able to zealously litigate on behalf of her clients.

Casey was previously an associate attorney at Whiteman Osterman & Hanna LLP, Albany's largest law firm, where she practiced primarily in the areas of Labor and Employment, Education and Litigation. Casey joined her mother, Anne Reynolds Copps, in practice as an associate with the firm in 2012 and became Anne's partner in 2014, creating Copps DiPaola, PLLC, the first mother-daughter law firm in the Capital Region. In 2018, Lorraine Silverman joined the firm as a partner and the firm name changed to its current name.

Casey regularly practices in the Capital District and surrounding counties, including Albany, Rensselaer, Schenectady, Saratoga, Columbia, and Schoharie. Casey also routinely travels as far north as Plattsburgh, as far south as Kingston, and as far west as Syracuse to represent birth and adoptive parents in adoptions. Casey is also admitted in Vermont where she practices exclusively in adoption and assisted reproductive technology law.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Casey focuses her practice in all areas of adoption law. She has experience representing birth and adoptive parents in private adoptions, voluntary agency adoptions, foster care adoptions and step/second parent adoptions. Casey also has experience representing adoption agencies and handling adoption subsidy fair hearings. Casey also practices in the related area of assisted reproductive technology law (egg/sperm/embryo donation and surrogacy/gestational carrier agreements) and kinship guardianship (KinGAP). Casey also practices in the areas of not-for-profit/for-profit/religious corporation formation and operations, estate planning and trusts, probate, real estate, landlord/tenant, employment law, education law and name changes.

Casey understands that many of her clients come to her during difficult and stressful times in their lives. She strives to educate her clients on the law and their options so they can make educated decisions about the trajectory of their cases. Casey understands that, while the matter that brings her clients to her are incredibly important to them, the vast majority of her clients have limited funds to spend on legal representation. With that in mind, Casey openly discusses with her clients the relative costs of various options and helps them to engage in a cost-benefit analysis.

Casey prides herself on being a creative problem solver and refuses to take a one size fits all approach to her cases. She spends time with her clients getting to know the facts of their cases intimately so she can help them brainstorm possible solutions to the problem that brought them to her. Particularly in matters involving families, Casey believes that working together to come up with a solution that addresses the needs and concerns of all involved to the best extent possible is almost always preferable to litigation, which can do irreparable damage to relationships. That being said, Casey has extensive litigation experience and, in the event that settlement is not an option, she is willing and able to zealously litigate on behalf of her clients.

Casey was previously an associate attorney at Whiteman Osterman & Hanna LLP, Albany's largest law firm, where she practiced primarily in the areas of Labor and Employment, Education and Litigation. Casey joined her mother, Anne Reynolds Copps, in practice as an associate with the firm in 2012 and became Anne's partner in 2014, creating Copps DiPaola, PLLC, the first mother-daughter law firm in the Capital Region. In 2018, Lorraine Silverman joined the firm as a partner and the firm name changed to its current name.

Casey regularly practices in the Capital District and surrounding counties, including Albany, Rensselaer, Schenectady, Saratoga, Columbia, and Schoharie. Casey also routinely travels as far north as Plattsburgh, as far south as Kingston, and as far west as Syracuse to represent birth and adoptive parents in adoptions. Casey is also admitted in Vermont where she practices exclusively in adoption and assisted reproductive technology law.

attorneys.name: Richard J. Dircks
attorneys.practice_type: Anti-fraud Litigation Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Richard J. Dircks, a partner at Getnick Law, is actively involved in all aspects of the firm’s dedicated anti-fraud litigation and business integrity practice. Mr. Dircks has experience representing individuals, businesses, and government entities in a variety of areas, including fraud investigation and litigation, False Claims Act qui tam litigation, IRS and SEC whistleblower claims, corporate monitoring/Independent Private Sector Inspector General (IPSIG) projects, and business litigation in both federal and state courts.

Mr. Dircks’ fraud investigation and litigation work on behalf of defrauded entities includes multi-million dollar matters successfully resolved in Federal and State courts for both domestic and international clients.

Mr. Dircks’ whistleblower practice, broad across industries and programs, includes groundbreaking cases and innovative results. For example, he played a key role in the successful civil prosecution of two New York False Claims Act cases that resulted in record relator share recoveries for Getnick Law clients while at the same time uniquely leveraging and expanding the reach of the NYFCA: the first was a consumer fraud case that led to a parallel criminal prosecution resulting in the payment of full restitution to consumer victims (in addition to the State’s FCA recovery); and, the second was an electric utility fraud case, the resolution of which included an agreement by the Government to use a portion of the case proceeds to provide utility-related aid to low- and moderate-income New Yorkers. In addition, Mr. Dircks was a member of the Getnick Law legal team nominated for “Trial Lawyer of the Year” recognition in connection with a $750 million case against GlaxoSmithKline that, for the first time, used the False Claims Act to hold drug makers accountable for selling adulterated pharmaceutical products to government health plans.

In the area of corporate monitorships, Mr. Dircks has held a number of leadership positions on significant Getnick Law engagements, including the World Trade Center Disaster Site Recovery and Clean-up, and the Federal-Court appointed monitorship over The New York Racing Association, Inc.

Mr. Dircks has organized or participated in a number of Continuing Legal Education programs, and has authored articles relevant to the firm’s anti-fraud and business integrity practice.

Mr. Dircks is a member of several professional associations, including the New York State Bar Association. Mr. Dircks serves on the Executive Committee of the New York State Bar Association Commercial and Federal Litigation Section, and for many years was Co-Chair of the Section’s Civil Prosecution Committee.

Prior to joining Getnick Law, Mr. Dircks served as the judicial law clerk for the Honorable James M. Ideman of the United States District Court for the Central District of California.

Mr. Dircks is a member of the New York Bar and is also admitted to practice in the United States District Courts for the Southern and Eastern Districts of New York.

attorneys.name: Sean D. Doddy
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
An accomplished trial lawyer and former New York prosecutor, Sean represents individuals facing high-stakes criminal prosecutions and investigations. Sean has successfully defended clients against a broad spectrum of state and federal charges and has tried numerous criminal cases in both state and federal courts.

Sean began his legal career as an Assistant District Attorney in the Bronx County District Attorney's Office, where he prosecuted a wide range of criminal cases, including several high-profile homicides. His recognized expertise in 2021 led him to a pivotal role with the New York City Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force, where he spearheaded multi-jurisdictional investigations into technology-facilitated crimes against children. The following year, Sean’s profound capabilities in digital forensics were further acknowledged when he was selected to join the United States Secret Service National Computer Forensics Institute.

Sean Doddy is a distinguished expert in criminal law, boasting an extensive track record in both prosecution and defense. At Doddy Law PLLC, he utilizes his deep knowledge of legal tactics and investigative methods practiced by federal and state law enforcement to craft formidable defenses and provide exceptional advocacy for his clients.

On the federal level, Sean’s expertise spans securities and financial fraud, cybercrime, and organized crime. He adopts a meticulous analytical approach to navigate complex cases, especially those involving sophisticated financial dealings and cutting-edge digital technologies. His profound grasp of regulatory landscapes and investigative strategies equips him to adeptly manage cases from financial misconduct to cyber offenses and digital forensics.

At the state level, Sean has a strong record of defending clients in New York State criminal courts across a broad spectrum of cases, including violent crimes, sex crimes, domestic violence, and juvenile offenses. His method integrates a thorough analysis of evidence with strategic procedural knowledge, enhancing his effectiveness in courtrooms handling cases from homicide to narcotics.

Sean applies the rigorous, expert advocacy that has defined his criminal law career to his New York family law practice. His experience as a special victims prosecutor, especially in severe cases of physical and sexual abuse against children, equips him with a distinctive skill set ideally suited to the complexities of family law.

His expertise in advanced investigative techniques and deep knowledge of digital forensics are crucial in handling family law cases involving technology-facilitated crimes such as online harassment, stalking, and revenge porn. These areas often demand sophisticated legal strategies and strong defensive actions.

In matters from child custody disputes to allegations of domestic violence and marriage dissolution, Sean's strategy combines thorough evidence review with compassionate, assertive advocacy. This approach ensures comprehensive consideration of all case aspects, providing clients robust representation aimed at securing favorable outcomes in intricate family scenarios.

As your family law attorney, Sean draws on his extensive criminal law background to deliver superior legal services, merging in-depth analytical capabilities with a dedicated pursuit of justice. Trust Sean to navigate the most challenging family law issues with precision and empathy, safeguarding your rights and interests in every legal matter.

attorneys.name: Teresa G. Donnellan Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Ballston Spa, NY
attorneys.bio:
Teresa G. Donnellan is the Partner of Donnellan Law, PLLC. Attorney Donnellan is a graduate of Albany Law School and has been admitted to the New York State Bar since 1992. She commenced her career with the Legal Aid Society of Suffolk County wherein she worked for the Law Guardian and Family Court Bureaus. After leaving Legal Aid, she joined the law firm of Schoenberg & Associates in Saratoga Springs where she continued to practice in the areas of family and matrimonial law until 1996, wherein Attorney Donnellan commenced her law practice concentrating on the areas of family and matrimonial law. Attorney Donnellan has been a member of the Saratoga County and Warren County Attorney for Children panels throughout her career in the Capital District and served as the Saratoga County Attorney for the Child Liaison.

Attorney Donnellan is an active member of multiple area organizations such as the American Bar Association, New York State Bar Association, the Saratoga County Bar Association, the Women’s Bar Association, and the Collaborative Divorce Association of the Capital District. She has been mentioned twice in the Saratoga Business Journal for her work with the Collaborative Divorce Association of the Capital District. Attorney Donnellan is a former member of the Board of Directors for the Open Arms Adoption Agency, an adoption network serving Pennsylvania, New Jersey, New York, and Delaware. She has had the honor of speaking to foster parents at Northeast Parent & Child Society regarding the role of Attorneys representing children in Foster Care. She has also had the opportunity to speak to SUNY Albany students earning Master’s Degrees in Social Work concerning the role of Attorneys for Children and the New York State Court System and to members of the local bar association with respect to ethics and the field of matrimonial law.

Attorney Donnellan continues to mentor students from Albany Law School who desire to learn about the field of Matrimonial and Family Law.

Super Lawyers has recognized Attorney Donnellan as among the top 5% of attorneys in New York. They are selected through peer nominations and evaluations along with third party research. Super Lawyers is a research-driven, peer influenced rating service of outstanding lawyers who have attained a high degree of peer recognition and professional achievement.

Mr. Donohue is admitted to practice law in the state of New York. He is a member of the American Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Patrick J. Donoghue
attorneys.practice_type: Federal Employers’ Liability Act Lawyers in Buffalo, NY
attorneys.bio:
Patrick J. Donoghue, Esq. started his legal career in 1998 after graduating from the George Washington University Law School. Prior to attending law school, Mr. Donoghue graduated with honors from SUNY Buffalo with a B.A. in Political Science. In between college and law school, Mr. Donoghue interned in the office of U.S. Senator Daniel Patrick Moynihan. During his career, Mr. Donoghue has solely represented injured people resulting from the negligence of others. Throughout his career, he has focused on representing injured railroad workers in cases brought pursuant to the Federal Employers’ Liability Act. This has been especially gratifying to Mr. Donoghue because five generations of his family have worked on the railroad. His uncle, Robert Donoghue, was a highly respected Local Chairman for Division 421 in Buffalo, New York. In fact, after his death, the Local was named in his honor.

Mr. Donoghue also specializes in representing injured construction workers under New York’s “scaffold law”, and he has handled numerous auto cases, trucking cases and premise liability cases. Mr. Donoghue has successfully tried cases to verdict in New York, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Massachusetts. He also has settled cases with successful outcomes in Ohio, Kentucky, and Tennessee. He has obtained numerous verdicts and settlements in excess of one million dollars. His goal in every case is not only to maximize his client’s recovery but also to make sure all of his client’s needs are met both during and after the case. Mr. Donoghue considers it an honor to represent injury victims and to help them through what is often one of the most difficult times in their lives. When not practicing law, he enjoys spending time with his wife and three kids, as well as playing the occasional round of golf.

attorneys.firm_name: Connors & Sullivan, Attorneys at Law, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Brooklyn, NY
attorneys.bio: NICOLE A. DONNELLY.was born and raised in the Flatbush neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York. Growing up with a Colombian mother, and an Irish American father, she was afforded the best of both cultures. Her first language was Spanish, and she learned English at school. Upon her graduation from St. Edmund Preparatory, she attended John Jay College of Criminal Justice. During that time, she was given the opportunity to intern at the Brooklyn ADA's Office which solidified her desire to become an Attorney. She furthered her education and attended Touro College, Jacob D. Fuschberg Law Center, where she graduated with high honors. During her time there she was an active member of the Latin American Law Students Association, and Phi Alpha Delta. Ms. Donnelly participated in the Disaster Relief Clinic to help Suffolk County residents receive FEMA Aid after Hurricane Sandy and participated in the Bankruptcy Clinic to help some of the same people affected by the storm start fresh. Her participation in those clinics gave her the opportunity to assist many Hispanic families. She was able to bridge the gap between clinic attorneys and clients who spoke Spanish. Ms. Donnelly also clerked with a Criminal Court Judge in Suffolk County Supreme Court to aid juvenile delinquents in rehabilitating their lives. Upon graduation she was offered a position at a Criminal Defense firm where she worked on white collar and RICO cases, it was at this point that she realized how much she enjoyed client interaction. Ms. Donnelly joined the Connors and Sullivan Team in June of 2020, a very uncertain time in New York with the hopes of becoming part of a team that could add some certainty to some people's very uncertain situations. Ms. Donnelly provides advice to clients regarding Estate Planning, Trust Preparation, and Medicaid, so that in a world of what ifs they have one less thing to worry about.

attorneys.name: Alvin Dorfman
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Freeport, NY
attorneys.bio:
Alvin Dorfman has handled personal injury cases from inception through trial for more than 40 years. His practice emphasizes personal injury, criminal, civil rights and civil liberties matters. His political activities have included running for District Attorney of Nassau County twice, running for the Nassau County legislature, and running for the New York State Assembly.

Mr. Dorfman is widely recognized for his impressive ability as an attorney and for his broad political involvement. Very notable in his background is his deep and abiding commitment to civil rights issues. Mr. Dorfman has been very active in defending civil rights activists, racial discrimination cases, freedom of information issues and integration issues.

In December 1997, a group of 100 tenants, mostly Hispanic, received word from the Town of Oyster Bay that they would be immediately evicted from a building complex in Hicksville. Al Dorfman represented the tenants in a successful legal challenge to the planned eviction.

In 1982 Al Dorfman represented the residents of a minority section of Long Beach against the advertising weekly called the Pennysaver, charging that the Pennysaver had engaged in a racially motivated economic boycott of their neighborhood. In 1984, as part of the settlement, the Pennysaver agreed to distribute the paper to the neighborhood.

In 1974 Mr. Dorfman represented Dennis Dillon, then a Democratic candidate for Nassau County District Attorney, in a suit against the incumbent DA. It was the first lawsuit brought under the recently enacted Freedom of Information Law.

In 1967, the only Black teacher at Baldwin High School, Maurice McNeill, was accused of molesting a 16 year old, white female student. The School Board pressed administrative charges against the teacher. A large segment of the community supported McNeill. Mr. Dorfman represented McNeill at the school disciplinary hearings that lasted approximately two months. McNeill was fully exonerated at the conclusion of the hearings and reinstated with back pay. The hearings were covered by the national and international press and the major broadcast networks.

In 1969, during a period of racial tension at Long Beach High School, a Black student was arrested and charged with desecrating the American flag. Al Dorfman represented the student. During the four day trial, one witness invoked the Fifth Amendment and refused to answer after Dorfman asked him if he had fabricated the charges. The student was acquitted after the jury deliberated only 10 minutes.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Allard K. Lowenstein Memorial Award given by the American Jewish Congress, 1984

CARECEN Pro-Bono Attorney of the Year 1997

"Long Islander who has made a difference" by LI Progressive Coalition, 1994

Kairos Award by LI Alliance for Peaceful Alternatives, 1997

John F. Kennedy Memorial Award by Freeport Democratic Club, 1975

attorneys.name: Matthew J. Dorsey
attorneys.practice_type: Estates & Estate Planning Lawyers in Saratoga Springs, NY
attorneys.bio:
Matt is partner concentrating his practice in the area of elder law, estate administration, and Medicaid planning. In his Medicaid planning practice, Matt works with families to preserve their assets, while obtaining access to necessary long term care services. Matt has been a Legal Services Provider for the Saratoga County Office for the Aging for over a decade and previously served as the Saratoga County Examiner of Guardianship Accounts. Matt is a frequent lecturer on elder law issues for the State and County Bar Associations, as well as the Office for the Aging and Community Hospice.

Matt is a member of the New York State Bar Association, Elder Law Section. He also served as an elected representative to the New York State Bar Association House of Delegates between 2003 and 2005. Based on Matt's professional background and long history of community service, the Saratoga County Bar Association nominated Matt in 2007 for a New York State Bar Association Outstanding Lawyer Award.

Matt's interest in the well being of our elderly led him to establish the Saratoga Springs Memory Walk for the benefit of the Alzheimer's Association in 1997. Matt served as Chairman of the Memory Walk from 1997 to 2001. The Saratoga Springs Memory Walk has been held annually since 1997 and has raised over $1 million dollars since its inception. In December, 2000, Matt was recognized as Volunteer of the Year by the Adirondack Branch of the Alzheimer's Association.

Matt served as City Attorney for the City of Saratoga Springs from 2004 to 2006. During his tenure, Matt acted as the primary staff person responsible for the City's purchase of six unique open space parcels, totaling 100 acres. Matt also drafted the first revision of the City of Saratoga Springs Ethics Code in over thirty years. Matt served as Special Counsel to the City in the defense of tax assessment cases between 2002 and 2006 and as Assistant City Attorney from 1996 to 1999. After leaving the City of Saratoga Springs, Matt represented the Town of Queensbury defending a tax assessment challenge case involving millions of dollars in assessed value. Matt has also successfully handled numerous tax assessment challenges for private landowners, resulting in significant reductions in their assessments.

Matt is a Member of the Saratoga Springs Rotary Club and served as Club President. He is also a Board Member and Secretary of the Saratoga Springs Rotary Education Foundation. The Foundation raises funds for and manages an endowment for the Rotary scholarship program, which provides over $40,000 in scholarship funding every year to area high school students.

Matt is a prior recipient of the Outstanding Young Leader Award from the Greater Saratoga Springs Jaycees. He is a 1998 graduate of the Leadership Saratoga Program, created by the Saratoga County Chamber of Commerce to develop community leaders in the Greater Saratoga area.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Outstanding Lawyer Nomination to NYS Bar Association Saratoga County Bar Association

Paul Harris Fellow Saratoga Springs Rotary Club

Volunteer of the Year Alzheimer’s Association of Northeastern NY

Outstanding Young Leader Award Greater Saratoga Springs Jaycees

attorneys.name: Steven Dorfman
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Steven Dorfman is a senior New York personal injury trial attorney at The Perecman Firm with nearly 30 years of experience representing victims of catastrophic construction accidents, wrongful death, traumatic brain injuries, and serious negligence throughout New York City. He is widely recognized for securing some of the largest settlements in complex Labor Law and construction accident cases.

Steven concentrates on high-exposure construction accident litigation involving scaffold falls, falling objects, structural collapses, crane accidents, and claims brought under New York Labor Law Sections 240(1), 241(6), and 200. He represents union and non-union workers and aggressively pursues recovery from owners, general contractors, and major insurers.

Notable Case Results:

• $29,950,000 settlement for the family of a 51-year-old construction worker who tragically fell 44 stories

• $19,000,000 settlement for an ironworker struck by a fallen I-beam

• $12,000,000 settlement for a teamster who suffered a traumatic brain injury, resolved before depositions

• $6,700,000 settlement for a pedestrian struck by a bus

• $5,000,000 settlement for a pedestrian injured in a school bus accident

These results reflect Steven’s meticulous case preparation, aggressive negotiation strategy, and deep understanding of New York construction accident law and wrongful death litigation.

He also served on the Steering Committee for the Metro-North Valhalla train accident litigation, helping secure justice for victims of the 2015 crossing tragedy.

As the firm’s only native Spanish-speaking attorney, Steven provides critical access to Spanish-speaking clients who may fear retaliation or uncertainty when asserting their rights. His advocacy focuses not only on financial recovery, but on restoring dignity and accountability.

Steven earned his B.A. in International Affairs from The George Washington University and his J.D. from Brooklyn Law School. He has argued more than 35 appeals in New York’s appellate courts and serves on the Board of Directors for the New York State Trial Lawyers Association. He is recognized annually by Super Lawyers and Best Lawyers, and his verdicts have been featured in the New York Law Journal’s Top Verdicts in New York.

Prior results do not guarantee a similar outcome.

attorneys.name: John Dowd
attorneys.practice_type: Veteran Appeals Lawyers in Newburgh, NY
attorneys.bio:
John was born and raised in the Bronx NY. He began his professional life in law enforcement when he joined the United States Army in 1972. John was initially assigned as a Military Policeman to the US Army Military Police Corps 519th Brigade at Fort Meade, Maryland for riot control duty in Washington DC. He was later assigned to the AWOL Apprehension Field Office, Philadelphia, PA where he was promoted to the rank of Sergeant and later awarded the Army Commendation Medal for meritorious service.

After his Honorable Discharge from military service he joined the City of White Plains NY Police Department. as a Police Officer. John then served in the Village of Scarsdale Police Department, where he was awarded several commendations including the Exceptional Duty Medal. John also managed the Police Department's National and NY State Accreditation Program. He retired in 1998 with the rank of Sergeant.

John graduated Manhattan College with a B.S. in General Studies, cum laude in May 1988. He was on the Dean's list and a member of Manhattan College's Epsilon Pi Honor Society, the National Honor Society, Alpha Sigma Lambda and NY State Regent's Scholarship.

He then attended Pace University School of Law and graduated with a Juris Doctor degree in May 1992. There his honors included Ranking Scholar, spring 1990 and fall 1991 and Pace University School of Law's Trustees Merit Scholarship for four years. He passed the New York and Connecticut Bar Exams in 1992 and is admitted to practice law in New York, Connecticut, the United States Southern District of New York and the Court of Appeal for Veterans Claims.

John joined Finkelstein & Partners in 1998 immediately after his retirement and has overseen and managed numerous personal injury cases including several $1,000,000 cases. In 2008 he became the Managing Attorney of the Finkelstein & Partners Veterans Services Group. John has been accredited by the Department of Veterans Affairs to represent veterans from all states. He has attended seminars held by the National Organization of Veterans Advocates in San Francisco in 2008 and in Washington DC in 2010. He also received training from the Veterans Consortium Pro Bono Program in Washington DC in 2008 and has since represented numerous homeless veterans. By desire, John's practice is now limited exclusively to representing his fellow veterans before the VA so that they may obtain all the benefits that they truly deserve.

John has been married to his wife, Denise, since 1983. They have two children, Meghan and Brendan. Meghan graduated from Cornell University in 2009 and Brendan is a Junior at The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

John holds memberships in the American Legion, Ancient Order of Hibernians (USA), The Benevolent & Protective Order of Elks. the, Knights of Columbus and the Police Emerald Society of Westchester County.

John now enjoys sailing, golfing and vacationing at his cottage in the County Kerry, Ireland.

Fort Meade Provost Marshall's

Top Cop Award, Department of the Army Commendation Medal

attorneys.name: John J. Dowd
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Law and Construction Litigation Lawyers in Albany, NY
attorneys.bio:
John J. Dowd, born in Troy, New York on October 25, 1972, is a magna cum laude graduate of Boston College (B.A. 1994) and a graduate of Albany Law School of Union University (J.D. 1997). He is admitted to practice in New York State as well as the United States District Court for the Northern and Southern Districts of New York. Mr. Dowd also is a member of the American Bar Association and the New York State Bar Association.

Mr. Dowd's primary areas of practice are construction law, general litigation, appeals, municipal litigation, business and commercial law, and real estate.

Prior to joining Dreyer Boyajian LLP, Mr. Dowd served as an Assistant Attorney General in the Litigation Bureau of the Office of the New York State Attorney General and was a partner at the law firm of Couch White LLP. As an assistant attorney general, Mr. Dowd represented several state agencies, including the New York State Department of Correctional Services and the New York State Police, in civil actions commenced in both state and federal courts. Mr. Dowd also tried several jury civil cases in federal court. While at Couch White LLP, Mr. Dowd served as a member of the firm's Construction and Commercial Transactions/Litigation group.

Mr. Dowd has represented a wide-variety of construction industry clients including project owners, contractors, subcontractors, suppliers, design professionals and surety companies. Mr. Dowd has extensive experience in contract law, surety law, lien law, construction trust law, commercial litigation, both jury and non-jury, having served as counsel in trials, arbitration and mediation. Mr. Dowd also is a member of the Associated General Contractors of New York State, LLC, the Eastern Contractors Association, the Northeastern Subcontractors Association and the Saratoga Builders Association, Inc.

Mr. Dowd also possesses considerable experience in defending commercial companies in massive tort actions involving alleged asbestos exposure. He also handles vehicle and traffic matters.

He resides in Saratoga Springs, New York with his wife, Marie, and his two children, Emma and Jack. Mr. Dowd has also been active in community affairs including coaching various levels of youth basketball, baseball, and softball.

attorneys.practice_type: Insurance & Reinsurance Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Sarah Downey represents and counsels primary and excess insurers in coverage matters involving directors and officers liability, errors and omissions, fiduciary liability, environmental and commercial general liability policies.

Sarah has counseled insurers on the interpretation of their policies in connection with various coverage issues including, but not limited to, late notice, prior knowledge, the insured versus insured exclusion, the contract exclusion and the conduct exclusions.

Sarah also represents insurers in coverage and bad faith litigation in state and federal courts. She is currently representing insurers in New York, New Jersey and Connecticut in coverage and bad faith litigation.

Sarah's coverage litigation experience compliments her coverage and monitoring work and has afforded her the opportunity to truly understand the importance of each detail associated with the handling of a coverage/monitoring matter. In addition to coverage litigation, she has defended claims involving employment discrimination and represents and counsels clients in matters involving various aspects of commercial litigation.

attorneys.bio:
Edwin Drantivy, Esq. strives for the highest degree of excellence in legal consultation, representation, and client relations with respect to matrimonial, business, commercial, personal injury, and consumer fraud matters. Mr. Drantivy upholds a dedicated policy to represent only those individuals and business entities that he believes in and he will only take on cases for which he is willing to fully devote his time and resources.

In support of his clients, Edwin Drantivy, Esq. pays great concentration to detail, allocates timely attention to his clients' personal and business matters of concern, focuses heavily on solving his clients' problems so that the complicating issues do not recur, and, most importantly, always keeps his clients exceptionally informed of any and all relevant progress on their matters.

Adam joined The Rothenberg Law Firm LLP in the summer of 2012, where he continues to fight for accident victims.
