attorneys.name: Barry R. Lax
attorneys.practice_type: Broker/Dealer Disputes Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Barry R. Lax, a founding partner of LAX & NEVILLE LLP, has an extensive background in commercial, employment and securities litigation in all forums, including, state and federal courts, and arbitrations before the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc. ("FINRA"), National Futures Association ("NFA"), Judicial Arbitration and Mediation Services ("JAMS") and the American Arbitration Association ("AAA").

Since forming Lax & Neville LLP in 2007, Mr. Lax has represented customers and broker/dealers in disputes regarding sales practice issues and product problem cases and has successful represented hedge fund investors and general partners in complicated commercial and securities litigations throughout his career. He has recovered in excess of $100 million in arbitration awards, judgments and settlements on behalf of broker/dealer customers and employees in the financial services industry, and has successfully defended and resolved numerous matters on behalf of his defense clients.

Mr. Lax has won three FINRA arbitration awards totaling approximately $2.6 million against Merrill Lynch on behalf of investors who were damaged by sales practice abuses of the Merrill Lynch Phil Scott Team. In one of the cases, Mr. Lax and his firm, who represent professional athletes nationwide, represented a former catcher for the Boston Red Sox, for sales practice abuses concerning the Merrill Lynch Phil Scott Team and the Merrill Lynch Phil Scott Team Income Portfolios. The FINRA arbitration panel awarded the full amount of his net out-of-pocket losses, along with the entire amount of the attorneys' fees and costs requested.

Mr. Lax has also represented numerous high net-worth investors regarding the systematic and firm-wide misrepresentations concerning the sale of speculative and highly complex investment products in arbitrations against Citigroup Smith Barney concerning the ASTA/MAT and Falcon hedge funds, Deutsche Bank concerning the Aravali Fund, and UBS Financial Services, Inc. concerning Lehman Brothers Principal Protected Notes.

Additionally, Mr. Lax has victoriously represented employees and employers in industry and private employment disputes, ranging from general breach of contract claims and failure to pay bonus claims to complex HIV discrimination and Qui Tam actions. Mr. Lax won a $1.2 million JAMS arbitration award for unpaid bonuses inclusive of interest and attorneys' fees wherein the claimant alleged that he received a drastically lower bonus than the one recommended by his supervisor solely because he was HIV positive and had recently gone on an approved medical leave of absence due to his illness in violation of the Americans with Disabilities Act, the New York State Human Rights Law and the New York City Human Rights Law. Mr. Lax also won a FINRA arbitration award against Morgan Stanley Smith Barney for failing to pay two of its current employees their earned back-end bonuses. The FINRA arbitration panel awarded the claimants the entire amount of compensatory damages they were seeking. Mr. Lax also successfully defended a well-known New York City restaurant and its manager against claims of age discrimination and defamation by a former employee.

Mr. Lax has also defended clients in regulatory matters and in avoidance and preference claims in Federal Bankruptcy Court. On March 3, 2011, Mr. Lax argued before the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit in the matter In re: Bernard L. Madoff Investment Securities LLC, regarding the determination of a customer's net equity claim against a broker-dealer pursuant to the Securities Investor Protection Act where the net equity claims were denied by the trustee. Mr. Lax was selected as one of three lawyers to argue before the Second Circuit on behalf of over 100 Madoff victims. Mr. Lax and his firm have been and continue to be at the forefront of the Madoff litigation.

Mr. Lax has been quoted extensively by The Wall Street Journal, The New York Times, CNN Money, Bloomberg, Dow Jones, Financial Planning, Thomson Reuters, New York Post, NY Daily News, Newswires Column, Investment News, WealthManagement.com, WNYC News, Long Island Press, Yeshiva World News and other financial publications. He has also appeared on television and radio news programs such as CBS News, NBC News, Court TV and Marketplace/NPR. He has also written articles concerning bonuses in the investment banking and financial services industry.

From 2003 through 2007, Mr. Lax owned and operated The Lax Law Firm, which also represented investors who had been damaged by broker misconduct, employees and employers in employment disputes and discrimination actions, and brokers and broker/dealers in customer arbitrations and enforcement and regulatory proceedings. Mr. Lax has been practicing in the financial services industry since he started his career as in-house counsel with Prudential Securities, Inc., and then CIBC Oppenheimer.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Syracuse, NY
attorneys.bio:
Emilee Lawson Hatch is an Attorney at Bousquet Holstein, PLLC. She concentrates her practice in the areas of estate planning, trust and estate administration, and estate and gift taxation.

She offers a strong work ethic and a high standard of service to the individuals she serves. She offers home, hospital, or office visits so she can engage with clients conveniently and on their terms.

Emilee prides herself on her practical approach to formulating unique strategies that fit her clients’ estate planning needs. No matter the size of the estate, her focus is on minimizing difficulties by preparing her clients and their families. Her work includes:

Wills

Revocable and irrevocable trusts

Health care planning

Tax and family management

Elder law

Medicaid planning

Probate litigation

Business succession planning

Life management assistance

As the author of the Trusts and Estates Survey of New York Law, Emilee’s knowledge is her greatest asset. She is proactive in staying informed of the latest developments in estate planning and administration law, and she puts those skills to work for her clients.

Emilee drafts individually tailored plans built on an evolving understanding of each client. At her law firm, the clients’ needs are paramount.

attorneys.name: Shaunna Lazzaro
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Shaunna Lazzaro is an associate at Levy Konigsberg, LLP where she specializes in representing victims of sexual and physical abuse, with a strong emphasis on individuals abused in the foster care and school system. Shaunna's practice concentrates on litigating claims brought under the Child Victims Act in New York State.

Prior to joining Levy Konigsberg, Shaunna served as a prosecutor at the Nassau County District Attorney's Office, where she prosecuted a wide variety of cases including assault, child endangerment, and driving while intoxicated charges. While at the DA's Office, Shaunna litigated numerous bench and jury trials to a successful guilty verdict. Shaunna also drafted hundreds of search warrants on prominent homicide and rape cases to enable a constitutional means to apprehend perpetrators of crimes and secure valuable evidence.

Shaunna's legal career has always focused on protecting victims and advocating for their rights. Her extensive experience interviewing victims of crimes allows her to bring an investigative and empathetic approach to the pursuit of justice for victims of sexual abuse.

Shaunna received her J.D. from Fordham University School of Law where she served as secretary and events coordinator for the Student Bar Association. Shaunna also spent three years as a trial advocate for the Brendan Moore Trial Advocacy Center where she competed in several mock trial competitions, ranking as a finalist at Florida State University's National Civil Mock Trial Competition. Shaunna also received her B.A. from Fordham College at Lincoln Center where she served as president of the Pre-Law Society and spent a summer working on a campaign for the New York City Mayoral Election.

Shaunna is admitted to practice in New York. In her free time, Shaunna enjoys exploring new restaurants in her neighborhood with her husband and their dog, Tompkins.

attorneys.name: Hon. Ferris D. Lebous
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Binghamton, NY
attorneys.bio:
Hon. Ferris D. Lebous served as a Supreme Court Justice for the Sixth Judicial District from 2006 to 2019. In 2020, he joined Coughlin & Gerhart LLP where he now collaborates with the firm’s fellow attorneys in the Litigation & Trial and other practice groups.

He was born in Binghamton, New York. He graduated from the State University at Binghamton in 1976, and the Benjamin N. Cardozo School of Law of Yeshiva University in 1979. After admission to the bar in 1980, he served as an Assistant District Attorney and Senior District Attorney for Broome County between 1980 and 1982. He then entered private practice, and was a member of the Binghamton firm Pearis, Resseguie, Kline, Barber & Lebous until his appointment to the Court of Claims by Gov. George E. Pataki on May 7, 1998, and served as Court of Claims Judge until 2005. He was elected as Justice to the Supreme Court of the State of New York in 2006 and served in that capacity through 2019.

Honors

Broome County Bar Association Stanley B. Reiter Award, 2019

attorneys.name: James J. LeBrou
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Albany, NY
attorneys.bio:
James J. LeBrou, Esq., is an Associate at Tully Rinckey PLLC and concentrates his practice in the area of Estate Planning, Elder Law, Real Estate, and Business Law.

Jim brings valuable experience in estate planning, business law, and civil litigation to Tully Rinckey. Prior to joining Tully Rinckey, Jim was an associate at an area law firm where he was involved in all phases of civil litigation including the preparation of pleadings, discovery, motion practice, trials and appeals. He also handled real estate, estate settlement, traffic violations and corporate establishment matters.

Furthermore, Jim has experience with trusts and estates from his work at The Ayco Company, L.P., a Goldman Sachs Company. At Ayco, Jim supervised a financial counseling service designed to assist individuals who had recently dealt with the death of their spouse or who were terminally ill. Through this service, Jim was significantly involved in working with numerous families affected by the attack on the World Trade Center in 2001. Jim also served as the company's first Chief Compliance Officer, where he supervised the compliance department and served as the primary contact for regulators (SEC, FINRA) during audits.

Additionally, Jim was the Department Chair of the Paralegal Studies program at Mildred Elley College, where he supervised the Paralegal Studies department faculty, served as an advisor to the students in the Paralegal Studies program, and served as an instructor for paralegal courses. He currently serves on the College's Advisory Committee and is an adjunct professor there.

Jim graduated cum laude from Union College with a degree in Managerial Economics. He received his Juris Doctor from Albany Law School, where he was on the Moot Court Board and Chairman of the Dominick L. Gabrielli Competition.

Jim is a member of the New York State Bar Association and the Trusts and Estates Section of that Association. He also has the Series 7, 9, 10, 24 and 63 securities licenses.

Selected to Super Lawyers Upstate New York list (top 5% of attorneys based upon peer reviews and other criteria) as one of the top attorneys in Upstate New York, Estate Planning & Probate, 2015-2017

attorneys.name: Eugene LeDonne
attorneys.practice_type: Copyright Litigation Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Eugene LeDonne is a partner in the New York office of Frommer Lawrence & Haug LLP. Eugene's practice encompasses all aspects of intellectual property.

Throughout his career, Eugene has handled complex intellectual property litigation at both the trial court and appellate levels. He has been involved in numerous suits concerning patent, trademark, copyright, trade-secret and related antitrust claims.

Eugene's practice also includes client counselling on patent prosecution and patent opinion matters. This aspect of his practice covers a broad range of industry sectors including optics, semiconductors, communications, medical devices, imaging, Internet applications and software.

Eugene has also served as a counselor and negotiator in a number of business settings. Throughout his career, Eugene has received significant settlement and licensing fees for his clients.

attorneys.name: John Leifert
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in White Plains, NY
attorneys.bio:
For over two decades, John has been litigating cases in Federal, state and municipal courts throughout New York and New Jersey. During that time, John has handled a diverse array of matters, including negligence cases, the defense of hospitals and physicians, and a broad range of health care disputes.

After growing up on Long Island, John opted for a ski jacket and gloves, choosing to live in Upstate New York for the next seven years as he attended college in Albany and law school in Buffalo. While awaiting admission to practice law, John assisted a Special Prosecutor in Niagara County to obtain a guilty verdict in a high-profile murder trial, thereby cementing his passion for litigation and the courtroom. John then returned to the New York metropolitan area, where he has remained ever since.

John is a seasoned, versatile litigator comfortable representing both plaintiffs and defendants. On the plaintiffs’ side, he helped obtain numerous verdicts and settlements including a multi-million-dollar award for the victim of an ATV accident. On the defense side, he has helped to secure numerous dismissals, including an award of summary judgment for a large hospital accused of psychiatric malpractice resulting in a patient’s severe facial disfigurement, and the loss of an eye.

John lives in Mamaroneck with his wife (a school teacher in Rye Neck), and their two children.

attorneys.name: Brian S. Lent Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio: Brian S. Lent served as the Managing Attorney for the Zurich American Staff Legal office. He had previously served as Chief Trial Counsel and Senior Trial Attorney for several other house counsel offices. Mr. Lent has tried more than 75 civil jury cases involving arson, assault, construction accidents, construction defects, premises liability products liability, automobile accidents, veterinary malpractice and professional responsibility. He obtained his Juris Doctorate from New York Law School in 1984, is a member of the New York State Bar and is admitted to practice in the United States District Courts for the Southern and Eastern Districts. Mr. Lent has successfully argued appeals before the Appellate Division in both the First and Second Departments. He also authored the motion leading to the Court of Appeals decision in Narducci v. Manhasset Bay Assoc., 96 N.Y.2d 259, which significantly curtailed the types of accidents covered by New York Labor Law section 240. Since becoming associated with the firm, Mr. Lent has obtained a directed verdict in a Kings County slip and fall case, which was later settled by the remaining defendant for $175,000. He also tried a Nassau County trip and fall case where the plaintiff alleged the existence of a defective staircase and insufficient lighting as the cause for his accident. The jury returned a liability verdict of 63% against the plaintiff for comparative fault.

attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Law Lawyers in Newburgh, NY
attorneys.bio:
Jeffrey C. Leo holds a Juris Doctorate from New York Law. Jeffrey attended Pace University and graduated with a Bachelor in Arts degree. Possessing a strong belief that communication is a key component in being an effective attorney, he majored in English and Speech Communication. He is licensed to practice in the state of New York.

Jeffrey has spent over 20 years practicing law and maximizing the rights of injured workers in the state of New York. During that time, he has represented thousands of claimants in their NYS Workers Compensation and Social Security Disability claims, respectively. He has a firm understanding of when to use diplomacy and when to be assertive. Jeffrey strives to provide clear communication to his clients so that they understand the law, the process, their obligations and the strategy of their claim. “The only way my client can make the best decision for their unique situation is to fully know and understand all of the relevant facts, those that are advantageous as well disadvantageous, and to weigh them accordingly.” He has a full appreciation for his clients and the adversity of their situations. He is dedicated to zealously representing his clients and to obtaining the favorable results for them.

When he is not strategizing on behalf of his clients, he is a devoted husband and father. He is very active in his child’s Catholic school and church. Additionally, Jeffrey has always been an extraordinary, animal lover and he continues to provide consistent donations and volunteering for local animal shelters. Jeffrey enjoys lifting weights, hot yoga and the martial arts; he has studied Taekwondo, Hapkido, Aikido, and he is currently studying Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu.

attorneys.name: Rosemary F. Lepiane
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce and Family Law Lawyers in Syracuse, NY
attorneys.bio:
Going through a divorce or family court matter is often intimidating and overwhelming. In times like this you need an attorney who will listen and one you can trust. My goal in any matter is to ensure that you feel supported and confident through this difficult time, all the while providing the best possible legal counsel.

Rosemary has been practicing law for 14 years. She now brings her years of experience to Bousquet Holstein where she handles civil matters with a focus on family court, divorce litigation and resolution. She has worked with clients in drafting separation and prenup agreements. She is also a member of the CNY Collaborative Family Law Professionals which seeks to resolve cases in a collaborative matter instead of litigation. She is also trained in Mediation. When a resolution cannot be reached she has litigated all aspects of divorce cases from evaluating assets and equitable distribution to spousal/child support and custody. Rosemary is also an experienced criminal attorney having handled numerous criminal matters, including traffic and DWI cases, since her admittance to the bar in 2005. Her practical and realistic approach to all of her cases makes her stand out from her peers.

Rosemary has also worked with clients from all backgrounds including, domestic violence situations. Since family and divorce matters are often complex, she also has experience with real estate law, tax lax and bankruptcy as they relate to divorce matters. Rosemary cares strongly about children and making sure they have a voice in the court system. She has represented children in complex and highly contested custody matters. She has fought zealously for children representing them in abuse and neglect matters.

Rosemary is involved in her community and currently sits on the Assigned Counsel Panel Board of Directors where she serves as secretary to the Board. This organization ensures that all people have a right to an attorney at every stage in criminal proceedings.

Rosemary was born and raised in Syracuse. She is a graduate of St. John Fisher College (Cum Laude) and Syracuse University College of Law. She has served as Assistant Corporation Counsel for the City of Syracuse where she handled complex civil ligation in both Supreme and Federal Court. During her tenure as an Assistant Corporation Counsel she successfully defended the City against a 40-million-dollar civil suit. She was also a Hearing Examiner for the City of Syracuse. While in law school Rosemary interned for the Onondaga County District Attorney’s office.

Her student Note, A Business Doing Pleasure: Combatting Sex Trafficking by Decriminalizing Sex Work, which advocates for labor and employment rights in the sex industry, was published in JCRED’s Volume 36, Winter 2023, Issue 3. While in law school Annalise also competed as a member of the Moot Court Honor Society, winning Best Oral Advocate at the Reardon Moot Court Competition and finishing as a quarterfinalist in the New York University Immigration Law Moot Court Competition.

Prior to law school, Annalise spent three years in Singapore earning a Master of Fine Arts in Film Production from New York University's Tisch School of the Arts, Asia before freelancing in various capacities in the film and television industry in New York and Los Angeles. She earned her Bachelor of Arts in American Studies from Rutgers University summa cum laude.

attorneys.name: Kimberly D. Lerner
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Carle Place, NY
attorneys.bio:
Kimberly began her career working at Brown & Wood, LLP, a large firm in New York City. In 2002, she joined the Nassau County District Attorney's Office where she tried numerous cases to verdict. She joined her father Richard's practice in 2005.

At Lerner & Lerner, P.C., she handles most of the criminal matters, including felonies, misdemeanors, and traffic violations, and assists Richard with all other matters. She is active in the Nassau County Bar Association and served on the Board of Directors from 2010-2013. She also formerly served as the head of its District Court Committee. Currently, she has been given the honor of serving on both the grievance committee and judiciary committee of the Nassau County Bar Association. Kimberly lectures frequently to members of the Nassau County Bar Association and was chosen by Senator Fuscillo to speak to high school students about DWI.

Ms. Lerner is a featured legal correspondent for a variety of national news programs, including Fox News, CNN and MSNBC and other local television news programs. She has appeared on numerous shows including The O'Reilly Factor, Hannity & Colmes, The Line Up, Scarborough Country, Live with Rita Cosby, Fox News Live, The Live Desk, Kendall's Court, Studio B with Sheppard Smith, Nancy Grace, The Big Story with John Gibson, The Strategy Room, The Neil Cavuto Show and Lou Dobbs. Channel 12 News, NBC News, CBS News, Fox News and ABC News.

Kimberly holds the prestigious AV Preeminent rating from Martindale-Hubbell, and was selected to the list of Super Lawyer's Rising Stars in New York for 2013.

attorneys.name: Maria C. Lesinski
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate & Business Law Lawyers in Syracuse, NY
attorneys.bio:
Maria advises in the areas of business and corporate law, bringing with her prior experience working in-house at some of the world’s leading media companies. In addition to general corporate matters, Maria specializes in trademark, copyright, defamation, rights of privacy, and publicity issues. She now uses her expertise to serve Newman & Lickstein’s individual and corporate clients.

After graduating cum laude from Syracuse University College of Law, where she concurrently earned her Master’s in TV, Radio and Film from the Newhouse School, Maria went on to work at Disney/ABC, FremantleMedia and Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM) Studios, earning her grit negotiating and drafting a wide range of commercial, talent, production, and intellectual property agreements for well-known unscripted television projects, and their executive producers, directors, talent, and production partners. She is also well-versed in advertising, marketing, production, and general entertainment compliance and legal issues. Prior to joining the firm Maria proudly served as the point production legal contact for MGM Studios’ Emmy Award-winning television show Shark Tank, where she worked closely with physical production managers, producers, entrepreneurs, and talent, supervising all aspects of the day-to-day legal needs of the show.

Maria was born and raised in Buffalo, NY. After residing for a time in New York, New York, and Los Angeles, California, she made the decision to return to Syracuse in 2022 with her partner, Benjamin, and their rescue bulldog, Howard.

attorneys.bio:
Joseph H. Lessem joined Graubard Miller in January 2005. Previously, he was a partner at Cowan, Liebowitz & Latman, P.C. and Special Counsel to Gursky & Ederer, LLP. Joe has extensive experience litigating intellectual property, real estate, antitrust, and commercial cases in federal and state courts, the U.S. International Trade Commission and arbitral tribunals. Joe's reported cases include:

Kwan v. Schlein, 634 F.3d 224 (2d Cir. 2011)

Rosenthal v. Quadriga Art, Inc., 69 A.D.3d 504, 894 N.Y.S.2d 32 (1st Dep't 2010)

Independence Community Bank v. East 86th St., LLC, 34 A.D.3d 219, 824 N.Y.S.2d 33 (1st Dep't 2006)

Markovitz v. Kachian, 28 A.D.3d 358, 814 N.Y.S.2d 60 (1st Dep't 2006)

Tommy Hilfiger Licensing, Inc. v. Goody's Family Clothing, Inc., 2003 WL 22331254 (N.D. Ga. May 9, 2003)

Christian Science Bd. of Directors v. Nolan, 259 F.3d 209 (4th Cir. 2001)

Christian Science Bd. of Directors v. Robinson, 123 F. Supp. 2d 965 (W.D.N.C. 2000), aff'd on opinion below, 1 Fed. Appx. 157 (4th Cir. 2001)

International Star Class Yacht Racing Ass'n v. Tommy Hilfiger U.S.A., Inc., 146 F.3d 66 (2d Cir. 1998), on remand, 1999 WL 108739 (S.D.N.Y. 1999)

Forschner Group v. Arrow Trading Co., Inc., 30 F.3d 348 (2d Cir. 1994) and 124 F.3d 402 (2d Cir. 1997)

Marvin Neiman, P.C. v. Adar Importing & Distrib. Co., 243 A.D.2d 408, 663 N.Y.S.2d 562 (1st Dep't 1997)

Duell v. Condon, 84 N.Y.2d 773, 647 N.E.2d 96, 622 N.Y.S.2d 891 (1995)

Kramer v. Pollock-Krasner Found., 890 F. Supp. 250 (S.D.N.Y. 1995)

Vitale v. Marlborough Gallery, 32 U.S.P.Q.2d 1283 (S.D.N.Y. 1994)

Hofmann v. Pressman Toy Corp., 790 F. Supp. 498 (D.N.J. 1990), aff'd without op., 947 F.2d 935 (3d Cir. 1991), cert. denied, 503 U.S. 963 (1992)

BR Ambulance Serv., Inc. v. Nationwide Nassau Ambulance, 150 A.D.2d 745, 542 N.Y.S.2d 21 (2d Dep't 1989)

Posner v. Minnesota Min. & Mfg. Co., Inc., 697 F. Supp. 122 (E.D.N.Y. 1988) and 713 F. Supp. 562 (E.D.N.Y. 1989)

Joe is the author of "How to Prepare Copyright Registrations and Copyright License Agreements that Maximize Damage Awards and Effective Equitable Relief," AIPLA Mid-Winter Institute Handbook (2001) and "Consumer Surveys in Trademark Litigation: Are They Worth It?" Corporate Counsel's Quarterly, vol. 16, no. 2 (April 2000). He has been a guest lecturer on intellectual property litigation at New York Law School.

attorneys.practice_type: SEC Enforcement Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Richard Levan has substantial experience in the Securities and White Collar Enforcement fields, having previously served as Chief Litigation Counsel at the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission’s Philadelphia Office and as an Assistant U.S. Attorney in the U.S. Department of Justice in Washington, D.C. Richard is currently co-chair of the Securities Regulation Committee of the Philadelphia Bar Association. He is former Chair of the American Bar Association’s Financial Services Integration Committee, a national group addressing the unique compliance and regulatory issues confronting banks, securities firms, and insurance companies today. He has also served as a member of the Editorial Advisory Board of Securities Law360 and the Pennsylvania Securities Commission’s Attorney Advisory Board.

Richard has over forty years of experience defending civil and criminal cases initiated by the U.S. Department of Justice, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, the PCAOB, state securities and insurance agencies and self-regulatory organizations such as FINRA. A seasoned trial attorney, Richard has tried over 60 cases to verdict. His extensive experience, judgment and tenacity make him a formidable advocate.

Richard writes frequently on matters affecting the securities industry and has been quoted in many publications, including The Wall Street Journal, The American Banker, Business Week, Bloomberg News, Smart Money, IA Week, The National Law Journal and Dow Jones News Service. He has also appeared on CNN and NBC Nightly News.

Richard has served as a featured speaker at national compliance and regulatory conferences sponsored by such organizations as the National Society of Compliance Professionals, National Regulatory Services, American Bar Association, Society of Financial Service Professionals, NASD/Wharton Institute, Pennsylvania Bar Institute and Investment Adviser Week. Richard has been listed in Pennsylvania Super Lawyers in the field of securities litigation since 2010. Richard also holds an AV rating, the highest rating awarded by Martindale-Hubbell.

attorneys.name: Jill Levi
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Jill Levi has more than thirty years of experience in all aspects of commercial litigation, business disputes, aviation financing disputes and construction litigation. Jill also practices in the area of aircraft financing, related corporate and commercial transactions and creditor’s rights. Jill also heads up the firm’s matrimonial practice. Jill obtained her B.A. from Queens College of the City University of New York summa cum laude in 1979 where she was admitted to Phi Beta Kappa. Jill earned her law degree with distinction from Hofstra University where she was an associate editor of the Law Review. Jill graduated as number two in her class. Jill has been named a Super Lawyer in Commercial Business Litigation from 2013 to 2017.

Jill was admitted to the New York Bar in 1983 and began her practice in the litigation department of Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison, LLP. Prior to founding Todd & Levi, LLP, Jill was a litigation partner at Feltman, Karesh, Major and Farbman.

Jill is admitted to practice in the New York State Courts, the United States District Court for the Southern and Eastern Districts of New York, and the United States Courts of Appeal for the Second, Third and Fifth Circuits.

Jill represents some of the largest electrical material suppliers in the country, and has advised clients on all matters involving a wide range of disputes in the construction industry. Jill is experienced in counseling clients on the most practical way to protect their interests prior to and after the commencement of litigation. Jill has vast expertise in advising construction clients on their pre-litigation remedies, such as filing liens and bond claims and representing clients in all matters of litigation in state and federal courts.

attorneys.name: Michele R. Levin
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Jericho, NY
attorneys.bio:
Michele Levin graduated Cum Laude from Binghamton University in 1993 and Hofstra University School of Law where she was a member of the Labor Law Journal and graduated with Dean’s List distinction in 1996. She is admitted to practice before the Courts of the State of New York and the United States District Courts for the Eastern and Southern Districts of New York.

Ms. Levin is a skilled litigator whose practice is concentrated in the defense of complex litigation matters and professional liability claims. She serves as defense counsel for physicians, podiatrists, optometrists, and other medical providers; health care facilities, nursing homes, and home health care agencies. She also serves as lead counsel for national medical providers in multi-district litigation matters. Known for her attention to detail and her commitment to her clients, Ms. Levin’s record of success in her twenty years of practice is unparalleled. She has excelled in obtaining both pre-trial dismissals, favorable jury verdicts, and appellate division decisions. Based on her experience, she is able to counsel her health care clients in a wide range of risk management areas and strategies.

Martindale Hubbell has rated her AV Preeminent, which is the highest possible rating in both legal ability and ethical standards, and Hofstra University School of Law awarded her the Outstanding Women in Law Award in 2017. She has authored professional articles and given lectures related to professional liability risk management and defense. She is a member of the New York State Bar Association, the Nassau County Bar Association, and the Defense Research Institute.

attorneys.name: Mitchell B. Levine Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial and Business Litigation Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Mitchell B. Levine is a trial attorney, both in New York as well as New Jersey, since 1992. He received his B.S. from Trenton State College (now known as The College of New Jersey) and his Juris Doctorate from The University of Bridgeport School of Law. Mr. Levine is also licensed to practice in the Southern and Eastern Districts of the New York Federal Courts, the Federal District Courts in New Jersey, the Third Circuit Court of Appeals and the United States Supreme Court. Mr. Levine's practice encompasses two distinct fields of law: the defense of personal injury/ general liability claims and commercial/business litigation. He most recently served as Counsel to the country's second largest cleaning and maintenance contractor defending, coordinating and overseeing the defense of personal injury lawsuits in 19 states, as well as prosecuting and defending commercial lawsuits involving the company. Further, Mr. Levine drafted many of the company's current indemnity and insurance provisions in order to reduce, shift or eliminate its legal exposure. Mr. Levine has extensive experience in the defense of premises and auto liability claims for several insurance carriers, third party administrators and self-insured entities. He has appeared in Court in every venue - both State and Federal - in the New York Metropolitan area successfully arguing cases before both the New York and New Jersey Appellate Courts. Mr. Levine is the author of an article that was published in the New Jersey Law Journal on civil procedure. He is also active in the community including serving as a Judge for the New Jersey State High School Mock Trial Competition.

attorneys.name: Michelle L. Levine
attorneys.firm_name: Gair, Gair, Conason, Rubinowitz, Bloom, Hershenhorn, Steigman & Mackauf
attorneys.practice_type: Catastrophic Personal Injury Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Michelle L. Levine dedicates most of her time to appellate work in catastrophic personal injury and medical malpractice cases. After over a decade focusing on corporate litigation-related and advisory matters, Ms. Levine decided to follow her passion for assisting others during their most personally challenging times.

Ms. Levine began her career at a major corporate law firm, where she gained broad experience in commercial litigation, international arbitration, and insurance matters in federal and state courts across the country. Her practice included appellate work in various industries and jurisdictions, including several submissions to the U.S. Supreme Court. Ms. Levine also spent significant time defending pro bono clients in immigration and housing court, including extensive briefing and arguments to support those in true need of justice. She then worked for several years in the legal department of a leading global bank, including preparing reports on significant litigation and investigations for senior management, and advising on the applicability of international securities regulations in the Global Wealth Management division. During Ms. Levine’s time in the corporate sector, she developed an ability to analyze complex legal issues and propose creative solutions - skills that she continues to incorporate into her writing and advocacy for clients of the firm.

Ms. Levine graduated from Northwestern University in 2004 and received her law degree from Duke Law School in 2007, where she was the Managing Editor of the Duke Law Journal. While in law school, she also spent a summer interning for Judge Richard J. Holwell in the U.S. District Court, Southern District of New York. She is admitted to practice in New York (2008) and the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York (2009).

Ms. Levine also spent significant time defending pro bono clients in immigration and housing court, including extensive briefing and arguments to support those in true need of justice. She then worked for several years in the legal department of a leading global bank, including preparing reports on significant litigation and investigations for senior management, and advising on the applicability of international securities regulations in the Global Wealth Management division. During Ms. Levine’s time in the corporate sector, she developed an ability to analyze complex legal issues and propose creative solutions - skills that she continues to incorporate into her writing and advocacy for clients of the firm.

Ms. Levine graduated from Northwestern University in 2004 and received her law degree from Duke Law School in 2007, where she was the Managing Editor of the Duke Law Journal. While in law school, she also spent a summer interning for Judge Richard J. Holwell in the U.S. District Court, Southern District of New York. attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Brooklyn, NY
attorneys.bio:
Avi Lew, Esq. is a partner at Korsinsky & Klein, LLP where he co-heads up the firm's Commercial Litigation and Employment Law department. Before joining Korsinsky & Klein, Avi was a partner at Warshaw Burstein, LLP. Prior to that, Avi was associated with a large national law firm and also served as an Assistant Attorney General for the State of New York.

Avi has extensive experience in all phases of litigation from pre-litigation negotiation and inception of actions through trial and appeal. His experience includes state and federal practice, arbitrations, mediations, trials and appeals. His practice involves a wide variety of matters including general and complex commercial litigation, contract and business disputes, employment law issues, real estate litigation, as well as construction law and Surrogate's Court litigation.

Avi's employment law experience includes representing employers and employees in matters involving discrimination, sexual harassment, breach of contract, retaliation, family medical leave laws, wrongful discharge, misappropriation of trade secrets, partnership disputes, etc.

Avi has published on a broad variety of subjects, and some of his articles have appeared in the New York Law Journal and Law 360. Avi has published on diverse topics including employment law and international law and has lectured on employment law.

Avi earned his J.D. in 1994 from Fordham University School of Law where he was an editor of the Fordham International Law Journal. He received his B.A. from Brooklyn College in 1991, where he majored in Economics, graduated summa cum laude, was inducted into Phi Beta Kappa and received the award for Excellence in Economics.

attorneys.name: Stanley J. Levy
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Stanley J. Levy is of counsel at Levy Konigsberg LLP. As one of LK's founding members, Stan has led the firm in building a national reputation as a leader in handling personal injury and wrongful death litigation involving asbestos, mesothelioma, product liability, hazardous wastes, contaminated groundwater, and other toxic torts. He has also expanded the firm's select areas of litigation to include pharmaceutical, healthcare, government, consumer, and commercial fraud.

Stan has over 40 years of international trial experience working on cases involving product liability class actions and aviation disasters. Of the latter, he has acted on behalf of victims of:

The air crash over the Ionian Sea;

The air crash near Staines, England;

The mid-air collision near Indianapolis.

For more than 20 years, Stan has been lead counsel in some of the nation's largest asbestos and mesothelioma lawsuits:

In 1990, he was appointed co-chairman of the Federal Judicial Center's Asbestos Litigation Management Project;

In 1996, he became a court-appointed member of the Southern Eastern Districts of New York's Civil Justice Reform Act Committee;

The same year he was appointed to the Joint Southern and Eastern District Local Rules Revision Committee.

After graduating from Harvard College in 1956 and Columbia University's School of Law in 1959, Stan served for four years as an Assistant Attorney General of New York. In that capacity, he investigated securities and consumer fraud, and was instrumental in the early regulation of real estate syndications under then-State Attorney General Louis Lefkowitz.

For more than two decades, Stan has been active on committees involving product liability, aeronautics, mass litigation toxic torts, and environmental law for the American Bar Association, the Association of the Bar of the City of New York, the Association of Trial Lawyers of America, the New York State Bar Association, the Federal Bar Council, and the Million Dollar Verdict Association.

He has served as Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Ray Tech Corporation and the U.S. Minerals Corporation, and as a director of the Manville Corporation.

A recognized authority on toxic torts and environmental law, Stan has frequently been cited in The Best Lawyers in America and in New York Super Lawyers.

He is the author of more than two dozen professional articles and has been a frequent lecturer for the National Law Journal, the Practicing Law Institute, and the Law Journal.

attorneys.name: Richard A. Librett
attorneys.practice_type: State and Federal Criminal Defense Lawyers in Garden City, NY
attorneys.bio:
Richard A. Librett is a 1973 graduate of the Albany Law School of Union University. He spent several years as a prosecutor until founding the firm with Lloyd M. Friedland. Richard has two children and resides on Long Island.

Over a long and varied career as a criminal defense attorney and litigator, he has been involved in many high-profile cases, including the Howard Beach case, the New York City Traffic Violations Bureau Scandal, the New York City Carting case, and many others including narcotics cases, money laundering and RICO. He has litigated cases in both the state and federal courts, representing large corporations as well as individuals accused of varied and serious offenses, and enjoys an excellent reputation as a concerned and aggressive advocate. In addition to his background as a criminal defense attorney, Richard has represented many corporations, officers, executives and shareholders in business disputes involving substantial assets and complex issues.

The firm's representative clients include substantial corporations and high net worth individuals, as well as local and small businesses. We pride ourselves in delivering a high level of service in a concerned and personal manner, tailored to the individual needs of the client.

attorneys.name: Scott A. Lickstein
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate + Business Law Lawyers in Syracuse, NY
attorneys.bio:
Scott is a long-term resident of Syracuse, New York and has been a preeminent attorney in the community for over 40 years. He has built his reputation and client relationships on the foundation of integrity, the proper application of knowledge, and honest assessments informed by years of experience. Scott’s “no-nonsense” determination to serve his clients has built relationships that have proven to be long-lasting and have extended through the generations.

Scott’s primary areas of practice include real estate, business and commercial law, complex commercial litigation, and leasing matters. He also has extensive experience in estate planning, estates, trusts and probate, family law, and asset recovery. Scott represents owners, sellers, and purchasers in real estate purchases, sales, and finance transactions for small businesses, retail centers, hotels, and other commercial real estates, as well as single and multiple-family homes. He also advises and supports businesses, charities, and other humanitarian outreaches within the community including lectures at seminars on commercial law, business formation, and account collection strategies.

attorneys.name: Stephen J. Lieb
attorneys.practice_type: Patent Litigation Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Stephen J. Lieb is a partner in the New York office of Frommer Lawrence & Haug LLP.

Mr. Lieb's practice focuses on patent litigation but provides a full compliment of intellectual property services for his clients, both to protect and assert their intellectual property and to defend against charges of infringement.

His litigation experience spans a range of technologies including electronic data systems, semiconductor processing equipment and fabrication techniques, pharmaceuticals, and gene amplification. He has represented a variety of clients from major players in electronics, pharmaceuticals, and biotechnology to small companies and individuals. He also provides client counseling and strategic patent prosecution services for clients in the electronics, computer systems, financial services, digital communications, and data encryption fields with an eye toward developing a cohesive portfolio rights.

attorneys.name: Daniel J Lieberman
attorneys.practice_type: Civil & Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Brooklyn, NY
attorneys.bio:
Daniel J. Lieberman as counsel to the firm brings with him in excess of 30 years experience in a wide variety of real estate matters, including without limitation, to residential and commercial sales and purchases, drafting and negotiating leases. and represents many lending institutions in New York. In addition, he has prepared and filed in excess of 100 cooperative and condominium offering plans with the NYS Attorney General.

Prior to joining the firm, Daniel was in-house attorney for one of the largest mortgage bankers in the metropolitan tri-state area for 24 years. In his capacity as bank attorney, representing many lending institutions in New York, he has advised many of New York's largest lenders on issues related to CEMA, Co-op and condo real estate. Currently, as lead counsel to one of New York's premier mortgage bankers, he has assisted the lender to navigate thru the many difficulties facing the lending industry, thereby assuring continued regulatory compliance with the rules and regulations issued by the various regulatory agencies.

Daniel is a graduate of Brooklyn Law School where he received the American Jurisprudence Award for excellence in the field of real estate practice.

Daniel is a NYPD Auxiliary Police officer for the past 13 years and is a certified team member of the Civilian Emergency Response Team for the last 10 years.

attorneys.name: Steven D. Lickstein
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate + Business Law Lawyers in Syracuse, NY
attorneys.bio:
Steven serves corporate and individual clients as their trusted legal advisor in business, technology, strategic matters. He gives reasoned, efficient, actionable, business-oriented advice to help clients achieve their goals in a pragmatic and cost-efficient manner.

He specializes in working with high growth and technology businesses, family businesses, private investors, and individuals, in matters ranging from business transactions, angel and venture capital investments, technology and intellectual property, and personal planning. Steven works with clients in all stages of their life cycles, from early stage startup businesses, business owners preparing for their next big move, and individuals seeking strategic legal guidance.

Steven brings with him the experience and approach of working at two of the country’s leading law firms in Boston for nearly a decade: Gunderson Dettmer, the world’s most active law firm serving the technology and venture capital communities, and Nutter McClennen & Fish, one of the most prestigious law firms in Boston since its founding in 1879.

While Steven primarily focuses his practice on helping clients with their business transactions and strategic planning, he is also an experienced litigator. His experience includes handling cases ranging from small contract disputes to complex matters with $30M+ at stake. He has helped achieve excellent litigation results for technology companies, manufacturers, real estate investors and developers, family businesses, consumer product and retail companies, and individuals in matters ranging from business and contract disputes, white collar criminal and regulatory investigations, employment matters, and intellectual property litigation. He also serves as local counsel in the Northern District of New York.

Steven is a native of the Syracuse area, and resides with his wife, Connie, and their three children in Jamesville, New York.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey A. Lichtman
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Negligence Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Jeffrey A. Lichtman, Senior Partner and trial attorney in the firm Trolman, Glaser & Lichtman, P.C. Mr. Lichtman graduated from the University of Notre Dame receiving his Juris Doctor Degree in 1978, and thereafter, was admitted to the New York State Bar in 1979. Mr. Lichtman presently manages the day to day operation of the law firm. In addition, he continues the hard work in the courthouse and is primarily involved in Medical Negligence, Lead Paint Poisoning, Labor Law, Product Liability, and General Liability. He has obtained numerous multi-million dollar verdicts and settlements in all of those areas of personal injury law. Many of the results achieved in the courthouse have received significant attention in the press, and have established precedent in the legal community. In addition to his commitment to each client's cause, Mr. Lichtman has for the past decade spent considerable time and energy devoted to protecting the right to trial by a jury in civil matters.He has served as President of the New York State Trial Lawyers Association and continues to serve as a Board Member actively involved in the politics of the profession.

Recent Cases

Mr. Lichtman represented two sons of a woman who died of complications after a gastric-bypass operation.This matter resulted in a trial and the jury verdict in the sum of $28 million dollars to compensate for pain and suffering and loss of parental guidance.

Mr. Lichtman represented ten year old twins who were seriously scalded and scarred as a result of hot oil that spilled when the kitchen stove tipped in their apartment as a result of negligent installation and proper support for this appliance.The matter was resolved before trial for $12 million dollars.

Mr. Lichtman represented a family of a young woman who sustained certain injury at birth leaving her brain injured and blind. Her twin sister was unharmed during the birth process. That matter was resolved before trial for $5 million dollars.

Mr. Lichtman represented a 65 year old woman who was injured in a motor vehicle accident sustaining significant damage to her left leg requiring multiple surgical procedures that resulted in a $800,000.00 settlement.

Mr. Lichtman represented a young woman in her 20’s who slipped and fell due to cleaning solvent in a drug store that initially caused ligamentus injury that lead to a complex regional pain syndrome. During trial, the matter was resolved for $2.4 million dollars.

Mr. Lichtman represented the family of an undocumented cement worker who was killed due to a collapse of the flooring at a construction site crushing him in the wreckage.The matter was resolved before trial for $2,500,000.00.

attorneys.name: Richard M. Liebman Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Law & Litigation Lawyers in Latham, NY
attorneys.bio:
Richard M. Liebman, Esq. is Of Counsel to the firm located in New York City. His practice encompasses a number of areas of law including commercial real estate financings, commercial real estate acquisitions and dispositions, corporate financings, Brownsfield transactions, commercial real estate lease transactions, mortgage loan portfolio transactions and commercial real estate loan originations and modifications.

Richard brings many years of experience to Tully Rinckey. He has a comprehensive knowledge of real estate, real estate financing, leasing, and Brownsfield transactions. Richard also brings retail commercial lease negotiating experience where he represented two major retailers and one major mini storage company in negotiating new store and warehouse locations.

Some of Richard's past casework includes representing a major life insurance company with a $55 million mortgage loan secured by four buildings, the purchase and financing of retail drug stores in 12 different states for $61 million, and representing a seller in connection with the sale of a New York City office building for $80 million together with all development rights.

Richard earned his Juris Doctor from Brooklyn Law School. Prior to law school, Richard received his B.A. with high honors from University of Denver. He also holds a Masters of Business Administration in Finance and Marketing Management from Baruch College-City University of New York.

Richard is an active member of the American Bar Association and New York State Bar Association. He is also the mayor's appointee as owner's representative for the New York City Loft Board.

Handled thousands of cases amounting to hundreds of millions of dollars;

Tried dozens of cases;

Settled hundreds of cases on courthouse steps;

Represented claimants and defendants;

Travelled USA, Europe, Asia, and Middle East for case work.

attorneys.name: Judge Joseph F. Lisa
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Mineola, NY
attorneys.bio:
Of Counsel To The Firm

Honorable Joseph F. Lisa is a former New York State Supreme Court Justice. He received his early education in the New York City Public Schools and holds 3 degrees, having received a Bachelor of Business Administration from St.

John's University in 1958, a Juris Doctor Degree from St. John's School of Law in 1960 and a LLM Degree from Brooklyn Law School in 1967.

He served in the United States Marine Corps Reserve from 1955 through 1961 and received an honorable discharge.

Judge Lisa was admitted to practice law in the State of New York in 1961. He served as Law Secretary to the late Justices William G. Giaccio and J. Irwin Shapiro.

In 1967, Judge Lisa was appointed Acting Chief of the Appeals Bureau of the Queens District Attorneys Office, and shortly thereafter, was elected a Delegate to the 1967 Constitutional Convention.

He subsequently served as a member of the New York State Assembly from 1969 through 1976, and as a member of the New York City Counsel from 1982 through 1991.

In 1992, Judge Lisa was elected to the New York City Civil Court and in 1993 he was appointed an Acting Justice of the New York State Supreme Court, a position he held until his election as a New York State Justice of the Supreme Court in 1996.

Judge Lisa was appointed Adjunct Professor of Political Science at City University of New York from 1993 through 1994 and has lectured and written extensively in both Europe and the United States on the social, legal, and ethical implications of the law in time of epidemics and pandemics. He is a permanent member of the scientific community of the San Marino Scientific Conference in the Republic of San Marino.

Judge Lisa is a member of the Association of Justices of the Supreme Court of the State of New York; Board of Judges of the Civil Court of the City of New York; American Justinian Society of Jurists; American Judges Association; Queens County Bar Association; Columbia Lawyers of Queens County; Catholic Lawyers of Queens County; and the Marine Corps League.

attorneys.name: Lawrence D. Lissauer
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Newburgh, NY
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Lissauer, who specializes in appellate advocacy, joined Finkelstein & Partners in 1996. He is considered by his peers to be one of the premiere appellate advocates in regard to construction accidents and trial appeals. Mr. Lissauer has argued appeals in all four Appellate Divisions within New York State and has handled cases of first impression before the highest Court in New York, The Court of Appeals. He successfully argued the matter of Riglioni v. Chambers Four Tractor Sales Inc., 2005 08243, 2006 01746 where summary judgment was denied to a distributor and a retailer in a strict products liability action, resulting in a settlement for the plaintiff. Also, in Alvarado v. Dillon, 67 A.D.3d 1214, the Appellate Division upheld an award to a client of the firm struck by a police vehicle. In Corwise v. Lefrak Org., 2011 01752 Mr. Lissauer successfully argued an application for leave to amend a pleading and to raise the addendum clause. In Kearns v. Adirondack Trailways, 59 A.D.3d 774. Mr. Lissauer successfully defeated summary judgment at both the trial level and at the appellate level for a client who fell while disembarking a commercial bus. In Butler v. Grimes, 2006 0551, Mr. Lissauer successfully upheld a multi-million dollar verdict on behalf of a client of the firm. In Casiero v. Stamer, 2002 06587, a jury verdict rendered on behalf of the defendant doctor in a medical malpractice case was overturned on a finding of judicial error, resulting in a new trial for the claimant. In Baez v. New York City Transit Authority, 15 A.D.3d 309, the New York City Transit Authority sought reduction of a verdict for pain and suffering and, after argument, the First Department affirmed the award of $600,000 for past pain and suffering and $380,000 for future pain and suffering. Mr. Lissauer has also argued successfully in many Labor Law cases including Cunningham v. Alexander King Plaza LLC, 22 A.D.3d 703, whereby the Appellate Division reversed summary judgment that had been granted to a general contractor. The reversal resulted in a large settlement for a client who fell off a ladder.

Mr. Lissauer has instructed many other lawyers on the subject of appellate practice through certified continuing legal education classes. Recently, he delivered a series of seminars to the Orange County Bar Association on topics including e-filing, construction site litigation, worker’s compensation and its relationship to third-party actions, assessing a trial transcript for appellate review and preserving a trial record for appellate review.

Mr. Lissauer’s motions and appellate papers have been included in form books and treatises used in the legal profession. He has also been involved in appeals and motion practice in the Federal District Courts of New York.

In addition to practicing law with the firm, Mr. Lissauer serves as an adjunct associate professor of business at SUNY Orange and has been on the college faculty since 1993. He has also served on advisory committees on paralegal development and is involved in the training of the firm’s paralegals.

attorneys.name: Peter N. Littman
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Binghamton, NY
attorneys.bio:
Peter joined Coughlin & Gerhart, LLP in 2026, bringing with him more than four decades of experience representing individuals and families across the Southern Tier and Central New York who have been injured through no fault of their own. His practice focuses on personal injury and workers’ compensation matters, including motor vehicle and truck accidents, construction site and workplace injuries, and claims involving toxic exposure and repetitive stress injuries.

Peter began his legal career after earning his Juris Doctor from Columbia Law School, following undergraduate studies in journalism at Lehigh University, where he graduated cum laude. He started his practice in California with a nationally recognized personal injury and class action firm before returning to Ithaca to continue representing injured clients in New York’s state and federal courts. Over the course of his career, Peter has tried more than 50 jury trials and handled a wide range of complex injury matters. His work is grounded in thorough preparation, clear communication, and practical strategy—an approach that helps clients understand their options and move forward with confidence during challenging times. Clients work directly with Peter throughout their cases. He is known for his personal, hands-on approach and for taking the time to understand each client’s circumstances, including the impact of an injury on their family and livelihood, in order to pursue the most effective path toward resolution.

Peter has long been active in professional organizations supporting trial advocacy and the rights of injured workers. He has held leadership roles with the Southern Tier Trial Lawyers Association and the Tioga County Bar Association and served for many years on the board of the New York State Trial Lawyers Association. He remains engaged in issues affecting access to the courts and protections for injured individuals.

Outside the practice of law, Peter has been deeply involved in the Ithaca community, serving with a variety of educational, civic, and cultural nonprofit organizations. He has long served on the board of the Elizabeth Ann Clune Montessori School of Ithaca, an experience he values as part of his ongoing commitment to the Ithaca community.

attorneys.name: Jeanne M. Gonsalves Lloyd
attorneys.practice_type: General Litigation Lawyers in Albany, NY
attorneys.bio:
Jeanne M. Gonsalves Lloyd is 1985 graduate of the College of St. Rose, cum laude, where she was the recipient of the Outstanding Scholarship Award in Political Science. Jeanne received her JD from Brooklyn Law School in 1988. Prior to joining O’Connor First, Jeanne gained extensive experience practicing law on Long Island, New York City and the Capital Region of New York. Jeanne is admitted to practice in the State of New York as well as the United States District Courts for the Eastern District of New York, Southern District of New York, Northern District of New York, and the Second Circuit Court of Appeals.

In addition to her 24 years in private practice where she has represented clients in general litigation, aviation defense, complex product liability defense, construction site accidents, motor vehicle accidents and premises liability cases, Jeanne also served as Claims Legal Counsel to Nationwide Insurance for 4 years, prior to becoming staff counsel for Nationwide for an additional 7 years. In her role as Claims Legal Counsel Jeanne evaluated coverage and prepared coverage opinions for the claims department on all personal and commercial lines policies. She also assisted and counseled claims personnel in liability and damages evaluations and monitored defense counsel in all litigated cases.

In 2000, Jeanne was asked to open Nationwide’s first staff counsel office in the Capital Region of the State of New York. As staff counsel Jeanne represented Nationwide insureds in a wide variety of personal injury actions pending in the counties located within the Third Judicial Department, including: motor vehicle, SUM, premises liability, construction site accidents, and dog bite cases.

In 2007 Jeanne returned to private practice where she has continued to represent clients in personal injury, premises liability and medical malpractice cases, as well as in general litigation, insurance agent errors and omissions cases, and insurance coverage cases. At O’Connor First, Jeanne focuses her practice in the areas of general litigation, insurance coverage disputes, and defense of complex personal injury, medical malpractice, motor vehicle accidents, premise liability and construction site accidents. Jeanne is a member of the New York State Bar Association and the Albany County Bar Association. She has been a speaker/presenter at CLE programs presented by the New York State Bar Association in the areas of civil practice, handling automobile accident cases, litigating construction site accidents, and insurance coverage.

attorneys.name: Anthony F. Lo Cicero
attorneys.practice_type: Anti-Counterfeiting Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
The firm's managing partner and an engineer by training, Tony has represented companies in patent litigation involving product areas as diverse as e-commerce platforms, angular rate sensors, refrigeration chemistry, camcorders and flat panel displays and in trademark matters involving clothing and shoes, candy, baby strollers, jewelry and many more.

He conducts due diligence of IP portfolios and provides strategic patent counseling to companies in a wide range of industries from recorded and published music to consumer electronics.

Tony is a past president of the New York Intellectual Property Law Association and is currently co-chair of its Legislative Action Committee.

Increasingly sophisticated technology competes with style and price as key aspects of the customer experience in the fashion industry. Tony represents some of the most prominent brick-and-mortar and online retailers in the country in patent disputes relating to the enterprise's e-commerce, mobile and point of sale systems. The retail industry regularly confronts patent assertions involving mobile platforms, electronic merchandise presentation, billing, marketing, inventory management and other features of the 21st century marketplace. He evaluates and responds to these assertions in a practical, business-oriented manner.

Tony also evaluates contractual terms with vendors and suppliers to mitigate liability and works with retailers to identify and obtain protection for their own innovations. He has assisted retailers in successfully pursuing indemnification claims ranging to seven-figure settlements.

Restaurants, financial institutions, insurance companies, health care institutions, consumer product manufacturers and other businesses likewise rely on technology to bind customers, improve the customer experience, differentiate themselves and stimulate demand. Tony advises clients on freedom to operate issues, prosecutes patents and defends them in litigation.

Many of the most prestigious apparel manufacturers and retailers in the world, along with financial services, food products, computer, consumer electronics, home products, and toy companies also turn to Tony for trademark protection.

He advances brand development and enforcement strategies ranging from anti-counterfeiting and trademark infringement protection to trade dress and Internet domain matters. For example, he overcame significant legal obstacles to protecting a name and symbol for what is now one of the best-known prestige brands in the country. On many occasions, he has been called upon to enforce trademark rights for entities that that do not have the advantage of a federal trademark registration.

In the public sector, Tony has been active in advocating responsible patent reform and he was actively involved in shaping the Trademark Anti-counterfeiting Act of 1984, and served on the board of the International Anti-counterfeiting Coalition during seminal efforts to strengthen the protection of federal and state laws, including Customs laws, to counteract counterfeiting. He is also effective at marshalling law enforcement agencies in the United States and other countries to disrupt and dismantle counterfeiting operations harming his clients' rights.

For example, counterfeit toner cartridges were adversely impacting the profitability of a major printer manufacturer; he coordinated Customs and law enforcement in the United States and abroad, obtained seizure orders and mitigated the problem. Similarly, he represents companies based in Europe, Asia and Latin America in protecting their trademark rights in the United States.

An important element of Tony's work is transactional and results in monetizing a client's IP through a sale or license agreement. Knowledgeable of customs and terms in a wide variety of industries, he counsels clients on structuring and pricing transactions when the IP is the key value of an enterprise.

Tony is a frequent speaker on issues of patent infringement, trademark dilution, anti-counterfeiting, arbitration, intellectual property damages and recovery, domain name disputes and Internet-related issues. He has been named a Super Lawyer for Intellectual Property and is included in Euromoney's list of IP Stars.

attorneys.name: Michael LoGiudice
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Brewster, NY
attorneys.bio:
Michael LoGiudice is a graduate of Brooklyn Law School (1997) and has many verdicts and settlements totaling over $100,000,000.00.

Michael handles all personal injury and medical malpractice claims. He also has a unique connection with municipality claims and construction accidents [New York Labor Law Sections 200, 240(1) and 241(6)]. Michael started his law practice by advertising “WE SUE NYC”. For years he built a reputation as a fierce adversary of all State, City and Local municipalities. For almost 30 years he has dedicated his professional career to representing all victims of police misconduct, civil rights violations, bus, train, auto, construction, work, sidewalk and crosswalk accidents.

Michael also brings a very unique perspective to construction accidents and N.Y.S. Labor Law cases. At an early age he was involved in his family’s construction and building maintenance business. He also has owned, operated and/or managed construction, roofing, painting and janitorial companies. Michael is OSHA certified and has taught and conducted many Toolbox Safety Meetings. In his prior careers Michael was a member of two local unions.

Recent settlements include a claim for a construction worker that fell over 20 feet to the ground in which Michael obtained a $11,489,900.00 settlement. Last year Michael facilitated a $3,425,000.00 settlement in Putnam County for injured driver.

attorneys.name: Amber R. Long
attorneys.practice_type: Mesothelioma and Asbestos Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
A partner at Levy Konigsberg LLP ("LK"), Amber Long focuses on asbestos/mesothelioma, tobacco and other toxic tort litigation. Amber is admitted to practice law in New York, New Jersey, and before the U.S. District Courts for the Eastern and Southern Districts of New York, the District of New Jersey, and the District of Connecticut, and before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit.

Since joining LK in January 2006, Amber has represented mesothelioma victims in lawsuits filed around the country, including in New Jersey, New York, Delaware, Minnesota, Wisconsin, and Louisiana. In addition to helping secure favorable settlements, Amber has achieved a number of victories on behalf of her clients at trial.

In November 2010, Amber acted as co-counsel to LK partner Jerome Block in a trial on behalf of a mother and son who both developed mesothelioma as a result of exposure to asbestos from automotive parts in their family's engine rebuilding and auto mechanic business. The jury returned a verdict of $1.74 million.

In December 2012, as co-counsel to Jerome Block, Amber helped win a $1.34 million award against a tobacco company on behalf of a man who started smoking as a young teenager, struggled to quit all his life, and died of lung cancer.

In July 2013, once again acting as co-counsel to Jerome Block in a case against a tobacco company, on behalf of an addicted smoker who started smoking before any warnings were ever placed on cigarette packs and advertisements, Amber helped secure a $5.5 million jury award.

In December 2014, Amber served as lead trial counsel in a mesothelioma lawsuit against a bus manufacturer. The jury's verdict, in favor of a school bus driver who was exposed to asbestos when present in the school's bus garage, totaled $7.7 million.

In January of 2019, Amber secured a $2.38 million award on behalf of a former New Jersey chemical company worker against a company that mined and sold asbestos to his employers.

In addition to her trial work, Amber is a skilled writer who has drafted a number of briefs defending LK's verdicts and has argued on behalf of her clients in the New York and New Jersey Appellate Division courts, as well as the New Jersey Supreme Court. In November 2019, Amber argued in the New Jersey Supreme Court on behalf of the NJAJ as amicus curiae in a case which will have important implications to many victims of asbestos exposure in New Jersey.

Amber was selected by Super Lawyers as a New York Metro Rising Star from 2014 to 2019 and as a New Jersey Rising Star in 2015 and 2019. Prior to joining LK, Amber worked as a Court Attorney to a New York City Criminal Court Judge, where she drafted judicial opinions and advised the Judge on both legal and practical issues.

Amber earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in Psychology from Cornell University in 2002. In 2005, she graduated magna cum laude from Brooklyn Law School. At Brooklyn Law School, Amber served as a Student Bar Association representative and was a member of the Journal of Law and Policy where, during her third year, she served as a "Notes and Comments" editor.

Amber is a member of the American Association for Justice, the New Jersey Association for Justice, and the New York and New Jersey State Bar Associations.

attorneys.name: David Lozner
attorneys.practice_type: Airline Accidents Lawyers in Brooklyn, NY
attorneys.bio:
Top Notch Personal Injury Attorney :

David Lozner is cofounder and managing partner of Lozner & Mastropietro. In addition to being a top-notch lawyer and negotiator, David spends his most gratifying hours at the law firm satisfying his clients' legal and individual needs.

The time following an injury is especially difficult for clients; typically, they have been harmed not only physically, but also financially and emotionally. David provides clients and their families with personal and professional guidance, counsel and support as they face uncertainty and fear after a serious accident or the death of a loved one.

David, born in Ukraine, immigrated with his family to the United States in 1981. After graduation from University at Buffalo Law School, David worked in the legal department of a major insurance company. He handled countless automobile accidents, lead poisoning injuries, premises accidents and construction accidents. Later, David became the managing attorney for the Brooklyn office of one of New York State's largest plaintiff's personal injury law firms.

But David's dream was to have his own firm. He had a vision of creating a law firm where clients are always treated with old-fashioned caring, respect and service, and where the lawyers are among the most successful and the most admired in the courtrooms and around the negotiating tables.

A decade later, his vision has become a reality. Lozner & Mastropietro is a haven for very satisfied clients. One of David's secrets to success is knowing which cases to fight until the bitter end in front of a jury and which to settle. It's an art, he says. Given his winning record, it is one he has clearly mastered.

At times my clients will ask me, Why do you recommend settling my case?' I tell them that artful negotiation can sometimes win them the same award that could be won at trial - except years sooner. The art is knowing which cases to settle and which cases to present to a trial jury. I know.

attorneys.name: Reyna Lubin Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Discrimination Lawyers in New York, NY
attorneys.bio:
Reyna Lubin is a fierce advocate for justice and a dedicated defender of her clients’ rights. As a highly respected trial attorney, she has built a national reputation for successfully litigating complex discrimination cases in both state and federal courts. Reyna represents individuals and nonprofit organizations harmed by unlawful conduct, with a practice focused on employment law, disability discrimination, sexual abuse, and fair housing.

Reyna has secured numerous favorable outcomes for her clients, including six and seven figure settlements in cases involving unlawful discrimination, sexual harassment, sexual assault, and retaliation. She has successfully opposed summary judgment motions in federal court for clients who experienced workplace sexual harassment and obtained favorable jury verdicts on behalf of clients who were subjected to discrimination.

Her recent achievements include:

Pre-litigation resolution of racial discrimination claims on behalf of a black woman against a multinational media company.

Pre-litigation resolution of a sexual harassment claim against a major pharmaceutical company.

Lead arbitration counsel in a racial discrimination and retaliation matter against a national food and beverage group that resulted in a substantial settlement for the Claimant.

Litigation on behalf of a woman in a sexual harassment matter against her former employer, a New York real estate company. The matter resulted in a favorable settlement for the Plaintiff.

Successfully opposed a motion for summary judgment to dismiss hostile work environment and retaliation claims brought by two former nuns against their religious employer.

Won a federal jury trial involving disability discrimination on behalf of a deaf plaintiff.

Won two federal bench trials involving disability discrimination.

Won two federal trials on behalf on a fair housing organization who uncovered violations of the Fair Housing Act in various assisted living facilities.

Drafted an appellate brief before the Sixth Circuit that expanded the statute of limitations for plaintiffs.

Prior to joining the firm, Reyna served as an Assistant District Attorney at the Kings County District Attorney’s Office. There, she prosecuted over 2,000 cases involving intimate partner violence, including charges of murder, sexual assault, firearms offenses, and unlawful dissemination of intimate images.

Reyna is a proud graduate of Louisiana State University. While earning her law degree, she was inducted into the Wex Malone American Inn of Court for her outstanding trial advocacy. As an undergraduate, she competed as a Division I student-athlete on the women’s soccer team.

A frequent speaker on issues of sexual harassment and fair housing, Reyna continues to be a leading voice in the fight for civil rights and systemic accountability.

Kristen joined Coughlin & Gerhart, LLP in 2007 and is a partner with the firm. She is chair of the firm’s Trusts & Estates Practice Group. She practices in both the main office and the Owego office, serving as the leader of the Owego office.

Kristen is a current member of the Broome County and New York State Bar Associations. She is a member of the New York Bar Association’s Elder Law and Special Needs Section. Kristen previously served on the Board of Directors to the local American Automobile Association (AAA) Club. She is a past Co-Chair of the Broome County Bar Association’s Young Lawyers Committee.
